
# System Documentation

## 1. System Overview

### 1.1 Purpose and scope

The GJC electronic wallet system manages a school-based token economy in which finance personnel issue and recover wallet value, merchants receive purchases and manage stalls, students purchase goods and transfer value, and parents supervise linked student accounts. The application identifies its release as version 1.0.0 in connection/config.php. Monetary presentation uses Philippine pesos and GJC tokens, with the shared conversion functions applying ten pesos per token.

This inventory describes the repository as inspected on 1 October 2026. It documents implementation rather than intended requirements. A declaration in a migration or a runtime schema helper establishes a repository-defined structure; it does not establish that the structure exists in a deployed database. Deployment state, external delivery, and behavior requiring execution are [unverified]. No application, installer, migration, worker, or database-changing operation is executed during the analysis.

All working-tree files, including hidden and ignored files, are included in the file inventory. Git internals are excluded because they contain version-control state rather than application modules. Text files are read in full. Binary files are read for size, signature, and integrity accounting; their visual, audio, and document content is [unverified]. The inventory does not reproduce credentials, personal records, uploaded document contents, or database seed records.

### 1.2 Architecture and technology

The system uses a server-rendered PHP monolith with direct PHP entry points. Role-specific directories contain HTML pages and action endpoints; connection/app.php supplies shared business and security functions; dedicated service classes implement circulation, minting, stall allocation, and tenant accounting. There is no repository-level application framework, ORM, central route registry, Composer manifest, or JavaScript application build manifest. PHP syntax includes the never return type and therefore requires PHP 8.1 or later.

PDO connects to a MySQL-compatible database using native prepared statements, UTF-8 settings, and transactional InnoDB tables. Database definitions are distributed among SQL installation files, an historical SQL dump, and PHP functions that create or alter tables when a feature is accessed. The active circulation calculation includes the treasury vault, student wallets, merchant wallets, parent wallets, and unredeemed legacy vouchers.

The browser interface combines PHP templates, Bootstrap 5.3.8 assets, application CSS and JavaScript, and externally hosted libraries. References include jQuery 3.7.1, DataTables 1.13.8, Font Awesome 6.5.2, jsQR 1.4.0, QRCode.js 1.0.0, SweetAlert2, Chart.js, and hosted fonts. References without an exact version do not establish a reproducible deployed version. QR image generation also uses an external QR image service. The repository contains PHPMailer 6.9.1 for SMTP delivery. There is no implemented external banking or payment-gateway settlement integration.

Apache rewrite and access rules are defined in .htaccess. The configuration derives application URLs from the request and repository folder and sets Asia/Manila as the PHP timezone. Database, SMTP, audit-account, and signing settings are supplied through environment variables and machine-local PHP configuration files. Secret values are intentionally omitted from this document.

### 1.3 Roles and authorization model

The shared role resolver maps role identifiers 1 to student, 2, 5, and 6 to merchant, 3 and 4 to finance, and 7 to parent. Historical admin naming is normalized to finance. Merchant ownership and staff membership are further represented by owner links and merchant_admin or merchant_staff subroles. The super_admin subrole protects selected finance operations, including minting and privileged audit or enrollment actions. A staff position is descriptive and does not independently confer permissions.

Student accounts own student wallets and enrollment state. Merchant owners own merchant wallets and inventory, while linked staff operate permitted owner resources. Parent accounts have separate parent records, separate wallets, and explicit parent–student link rows. Finance personnel administer cash movement, applications, accounts, leases, fees, and school years. Entry-point checks, operation-specific guards, and ownership checks collectively implement authorization; there is no universal controller middleware.

### 1.4 Entry points, configuration, and supporting packages

The principal public entry points are index.php, login.php, record.php, dashboard.php, logout.php, change_password.php, stalls.php, apply.php, and apply_upload.php. Authenticated pages reside under admin/, merchant/, student/, and parent/. JSON and action handlers reside in their api/ directories and in api/profile_photo.php. Some HTML pages also process POST requests or provide download responses, as identified in the module route catalogues.

connection/config.php defines paths, URLs, timezone, version, and environment/local-setting resolution. connection/pdo.php establishes the principal PDO connection. connection/local_config.php and its example define local application settings; connection/audit_config.php and its example define the separate audit connection; connection/mail_config.php and its example define SMTP settings. The contents of configured secrets are not reproduced.

The separate brag-output/composition/package.json describes a Hyperframes composition package, with preview, validation, rendering, and publication scripts using Hyperframes 0.8.73. Its composition uses GSAP 3.14.2. The duplicated brag skill packages under .agents/ and .claude/ include Python project manifests and uv lockfiles; their audio tooling depends on Python 3.11 or later, librosa, NumPy, SciPy, and SoundFile. These packages support documentation/media production and are not dependencies of the wallet request path.

## 2. Module Inventory

### 2.1 Public Access and Authentication

#### a. Module Description

The public module presents the service, routes authenticated users to role dashboards, and establishes or terminates sessions. Prospective merchants use the separate application module; account provisioning is administered through finance.

#### b. Features

Authentication. record.php verifies the submitted email and password against the stored password hash, rejects inactive or locked accounts, records successful and denied attempts, and establishes a regenerated session. Persistent login uses a selector and hashed validator, rotates the stored token, and applies a thirty-day lifetime.

Password transition. change_password.php handles the first-login or forced-password-change state and clears the associated flags after a valid update. dashboard.php selects a destination from the resolved role, while logout.php clears persistent login state and the session.

Profile photograph. api/profile_photo.php accepts a current user's image upload or removal. It validates JPEG, PNG, or WebP media, limits files to two megabytes, assigns a user-specific asset filename, and updates users.profile_img.

Inactive public workflows. register.php, registration_success.php, forgot_password.php, reset_password.php, verify_email.php, and verify_forgot_otp.php redirect to login. These files do not implement active public registration, recovery, or OTP verification.

#### d. Database Tables Used

- **auth_remember_tokens**. Stores persistent-login selectors, hashed validators, user attribution, and expiry. Raw validators are not stored as the verification value. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `selector`, `token_hash`, `expires_at`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **systemic_audit_trail**. Stores redacted actor/action/target events, old/new serialized values, request context, outcome, and chained hashes. User attribution is nullable for unknown or pre-authentication actors. Key declared columns: `user_id`, `log_id`, `user_role`, `action_type`, `stall_id`, `affected_table`, `old_value`, `new_value`, `ip_address`, `user_agent`, `timestamp`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **users**. Stores login identity, password hash, role/subrole, merchant ownership, profile, first-login flags, and account restrictions. userID is the principal identity referenced by wallets and role-specific records; roleID relates to role. Key declared columns: `userID`, `roleID`, `last_name`, `first_name`, `middle_name`, `suffix`, `contact_number`, `email`, `password`, `mint_pin`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.

#### e. API Endpoints and HTTP Entry Points

Routes are relative to the application base URL. The method notation identifies the request inputs consumed by the implementation; it does not imply a universal method-rejection guard. Where GET and POST are merged, both can supply an action. Each PHP file is counted once as an entry point; its action variants are listed separately.

##### POST /api/profile_photo.php

Source: `api/profile_photo.php`. Any signed-in user with a nonzero user identifier. Uploads the photo multipart field by default or removes the current user's stored photograph with action=remove. It returns success/error data and the resulting image information.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `photo`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `remove`: Removes the selected current-user image.
- `upload`: Validates and stores the submitted image.

Response: JSON success/error or message data; payload keys directly constructed include `success`, `error`, `photo_url`. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

No gjc_csrf_verify call occurs in this handler.

##### GET / POST /change_password.php

Source: `change_password.php`. Current login or forced-password-change session as checked by the handler. Presents and processes the forced password-change form.

Request fields read directly: `confirm_pass`, `new_pass`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

Response: HTML page or redirect with validation/session feedback.

Source: `dashboard.php`. Current login or forced-password-change session as checked by the handler. Redirects the session to the resolved role dashboard or required password change.

### 2.2 Shared Application Services

#### a. Module Description

The shared service module supplies the functions used by role pages, action handlers, and domain classes. It centralizes account state, wallet lookup, presentation conventions, schema compatibility, notifications, enrollment rules, and common transaction representations.

#### b. Features

Configuration and presentation. Environment values take precedence over local configuration. Formatting helpers produce peso and token labels, dates, ages, and addresses; gjc_e performs a string cast and does not HTML-escape its argument.

Session and ownership services. Role guards restore eligible remembered sessions, enforce account status and forced password changes, and resolve merchant staff to their owning merchant. Signed view tokens bind an identifier to a scope using HMAC; they do not replace resource ownership checks.

Account restrictions. Timed suspensions expire lazily, while bans remain until explicitly lifted. The lockout implementation tracks whether the restriction itself froze a wallet so that lifting it does not overwrite an independent parent-imposed freeze.

Product restriction matching. Product names undergo case, Unicode-lookalike, substitution, punctuation, token, and repetition normalization. Exact or contains rules and limited fuzzy token matching identify restricted products; rescans and strike thresholds can suspend a merchant operation.

Compatibility and bootstrap. Ensure-functions create missing operational tables, extend columns or enumeration values, and establish required indexes. The definitions coexist with historical SQL and do not prove that every deployed database has the same shape.

Shared business state. Transaction adapters normalize legacy and current ledgers for reports. Cart snapshots revalidate item availability and merchant membership; enrollment state controls student wallet access; notification and fee helpers record feature-specific events.

Signatures identify explicit inputs; handlers also consume enclosing session, request, DOM, or service state. ### 2.3 Finance, Circulation, Fees, and Cash Management

#### a. Module Description

The finance module supervises circulating wallet value, cash intake and release, tuition-related charges, fee-waiver credits, financial reporting, and operational settings. Finance personnel use the pages; selected cap and PIN operations require the super_admin subrole.

#### b. Features

Circulation accounting. CirculationEngine locks the system settings row and coordinates guarded wallet changes with ledger records. Its snapshot sums the vault, student, merchant, and parent balances and active legacy voucher value against the authorized cap.

Cash-in and service fees. The implemented system rate is one percent and the merchant rate is two percent. Fees are added to the requested base amount; a finance cash-in drains the vault for credited value, while the optional merchant cut also drains the vault. The school fee is recorded as cash revenue rather than newly minted tokens. Some historical comments describe different percentages; the constants and arithmetic govern this description.

Merchant-funded loading. Merchant-to-student and merchant-to-parent loading initially debits the gross amount, credits the recipient with the base amount, returns the merchant cut to the merchant, and credits the system fee to the vault. The merchant must satisfy the initial gross-balance check.

Cash-out. Merchant requests enter encashment_requests as pending without reserving a wallet balance. Finance release validates the pending request, invokes settlement to move merchant value to the vault, and then marks the request released. Settlement and the subsequent request-status update are not enclosed in one shared transaction.

Cap increases. MintingGuard rechecks super-administrator membership, requires a positive amount and reason, applies a monthly soft threshold of 50,000 and a hard threshold of 500,000, and requires the mint PIN above the soft threshold. PIN configuration verifies the current password and stores a password hash.

Fee waivers. Credits progress through amount assignment, signed-document posting, and one-time student or linked-parent claim. A claim increases the cap and student balance without draining the vault. The separate finance CSV path imports direct credits for existing students.

Maintenance charges. Configurable maintenance fees accrue for qualifying payments or transfers and are maintained separately from wallet value. Collection creates receipt records; an admin wallet view can automatically collect earlier-day charges. Reversal voids accrued charges, while previously collected charges remain recorded.

Reporting and settings. Finance pages aggregate wallet balances, transaction activity, queues, and circulation; downloads provide filtered transaction or fee data. Settings control transfer and top-up limits, restriction thresholds, waiver limits, and maintenance rates. Legacy top-up and encashment pages redirect to the unified cash-management page.

#### d. Database Tables Used

- **app_settings**. Stores named application settings and their values, with update metadata. Shared defaults supply values absent from the table. Key declared columns: `setting_key`, `setting_value`, `updated_by`, `updated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **cap_increase_log**. Stores cap increases, initiating users, reasons, and timestamps used by mint-limit reporting. Key declared columns: `id`, `super_admin_id`, `old_cap`, `new_cap`, `amount_added`, `reason`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **encashment_requests**. Stores merchant cash-out requests, requested amounts, status, and release attribution. merchant_wallet_id identifies the wallet validated during release. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `merchant_wallet_id`, `amount`, `status`, `method`, `reference_no`, `released_by`, `released_at`, `rejected_by`, `rejected_at`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **fee_revenue_log**. Stores system and merchant fee attribution against transaction references and amounts. Key declared columns: `id`, `merchant_wallet_id`, `transaction_ref`, `top_up_source`, `cash_amount`, `system_fee`, `merchant_fee`, `processed_by`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **fee_waiver_credit_logs**. Stores changes to waiver-credit state with actor and amount metadata. Credit or student identifiers connect each event to its waiver context. Key declared columns: `id`, `amount`, `fee_waiver_credit_id`, `old_status`, `new_status`, `changed_by_user_id`, `changed_by_role`, `changed_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **fee_waiver_credits**. Stores one student's waiver amount, workflow state, uploaded document, and claim/administrative metadata. student_user_id identifies the credited student. Key declared columns: `id`, `student_user_id`, `amount`, `status`, `waiver_file`, `claimed_at`, `claimed_by_user_id`, `claim_reference`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **maintenance_fee_collections**. Stores collection receipts, student and collector identifiers, amount, reference, and collection time. One receipt groups the collected maintenance-fee rows. Key declared columns: `id`, `student_user_id`, `receipt_no`, `entry_count`, `total_amount`, `collected_by`, `collected_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **maintenance_fees**. Stores assessed charges by student, transaction reference, amount, rate, and accrued/collected/void state. collection_id associates a collected charge with its receipt. Key declared columns: `id`, `student_user_id`, `school_year_id`, `status`, `reference_no`, `source_type`, `txn_amount`, `fee_amount`, `created_at`, `collected_at`, `collected_by`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **merchant**. Stores the historical/current merchant business identity and account/stall association used by compatibility access. Key declared columns: `userID`, `merchantID`, `stall_name`, `stall_id`, `operational_status`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `notes`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **merchant_card_views**. Stores finance viewer/merchant inspection timestamps used for directory review indicators. Key declared columns: `merchant_id`, `last_viewed_at`, `viewed_by`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **merchant_wallets**. Stores the merchant owner's balance. user_id identifies users; purchase, settlement, and merchant-funded load movements reference its wallet id. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `balance`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **parent_student_links**. Relates a parent record to a student user and enforces link uniqueness. This association authorizes parent supervision and allowance or waiver operations. Key declared columns: `id`, `parent_id`, `student_user_id`, `linked_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **parent_wallets**. Stores each parent's independent balance. parent_id identifies parents; transactions and parent shopping records can reference its id. Key declared columns: `id`, `parent_id`, `balance`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **parents**. Stores the parent-to-user association and low-balance alert threshold. user_id identifies users; parent_student_links, parent_wallets, and parent_alerts use the parent id. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `low_balance_threshold`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **school_years**. Defines named school-year intervals and the active-year flag. Enrollment, balance snapshots, and tagged transactions reference the year id. Key declared columns: `id`, `school_year_name`, `start_date`, `end_date`, `is_active`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **student_info**. Stores school-issued student identity, year level, course linkage, and graduation metadata for users. studentID is used for lookup and roster matching. Key declared columns: `userID`, `stud_infoID`, `studentID`, `yr_lvl`, `courseID`, `graduated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **student_wallets**. Stores the student user's balance, freeze flag, and spending controls. user_id identifies users; current transactions and peer transfers attribute movements to this wallet. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `balance`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `daily_spend_limit`, `is_frozen`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **system_settings**. Stores authorized circulation cap, cashier vault value, and related system controls. CirculationEngine serializes value-changing operations by locking its settings row. Key declared columns: `id`, `total_circulation_cap`, `cashier_vault_points`, `last_cap_increased_by`, `last_cap_increased_at`, `updated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **systemic_audit_trail**. Stores redacted actor/action/target events, old/new serialized values, request context, outcome, and chained hashes. User attribution is nullable for unknown or pre-authentication actors. Key declared columns: `user_id`, `log_id`, `user_role`, `action_type`, `stall_id`, `affected_table`, `old_value`, `new_value`, `ip_address`, `user_agent`, `timestamp`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **topup**. Stores historical top-up records used by legacy transaction adapters. Key declared columns: `userID`, `amount`, `topupID`, `adminID`, `wallet_id`, `remarks`, `date_time`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **topup_requests**. Stores operational student top-up request state and request attribution; its existence does not establish a current self-service request interface. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `student_wallet_id`, `amount`, `status`, `payment_method`, `reference_no`, `approved_by`, `approved_at`, `rejected_by`, `rejected_at`, `created_at`, `top_up_source`, `fee_amount`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **transactions**. Stores the current referenced wallet ledger, including type, amount, status, fees, initiating user, wallet attribution, and school-year context. Optional student, merchant, and parent wallet identifiers distinguish the movement. Key declared columns: `id`, `student_wallet_id`, `merchant_wallet_id`, `transaction_type`, `amount`, `status`, `reference_no`, `initiated_by`, `voucher_id`, `vault_before`, `vault_after`, `total_in_circulation`, `notes`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **users**. Stores login identity, password hash, role/subrole, merchant ownership, profile, first-login flags, and account restrictions. userID is the principal identity referenced by wallets and role-specific records; roleID relates to role. Key declared columns: `userID`, `roleID`, `last_name`, `first_name`, `middle_name`, `suffix`, `contact_number`, `email`, `password`, `mint_pin`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **vouchers**. Stores historical issued voucher value, validity, ownership, and status. Eligible active voucher value remains in circulation accounting. Key declared columns: `id`, `status`, `qr_code_hash`, `voucher_code`, `issued_by`, `is_refundable`, `visitor_name`, `visitor_contact`, `initial_value`, `original_amount`, `remaining_balance`, `expired_at`, `cancelled_at`, `last_used_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **wallet**. Stores the historical generic wallet model. Active role-specific operations use student_wallets, merchant_wallets, and parent_wallets. Key declared columns: `userID`, `balance`, `wallet_id`, `last_updated`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.

#### e. API Endpoints and HTTP Entry Points

Routes are relative to the application base URL. The method notation identifies the request inputs consumed by the implementation; it does not imply a universal method-rejection guard. Where GET and POST are merged, both can supply an action. Each PHP file is counted once as an entry point; its action variants are listed separately.

##### GET / POST /admin/api/economy.php

Source: `admin/api/economy.php`. Session required; finance checks apply to top-up/settlement branches only. See the operation note. Dispatches topup, topup_parent, settle, pay, circulation, lookup_student, and lookup_parent_by_student. Top-up and settlement branches require finance; pay, circulation, and student lookup require a session but have no branch-specific role or supplied-wallet ownership check.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `amount`, `merchant_wallet_id`, `notes`, `parent_id`, `school_id`, `student_wallet_id`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `circulation`: Returns the current circulation snapshot.
- `lookup_parent_by_student`: Resolves the student's linked parent and wallet.
- `lookup_student`: Returns the matching student and wallet.
- `pay`: Transfers the supplied student-wallet amount to the supplied merchant wallet.
- `settle`: Returns merchant wallet value to the vault.
- `topup`: Credits a student wallet from the vault.
- `topup_parent`: Credits a parent wallet from the vault.

Response: JSON success/error or message data; payload keys directly constructed include `success`, `error`, `name`, `user_id`, `wallet_id`, `parents`, `parent_id`. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

No gjc_csrf_verify call occurs in this handler.

##### POST /admin/api/fee_waiver_credits.php

Source: `admin/api/fee_waiver_credits.php`. Allowed role(s): finance. Sets a student's credit amount, uploads the signed waiver, cancels an eligible pending credit, or returns detail. The recipient is identified by student_user_id. The upload field is waiver.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `amount`, `student_user_id`, `waiver`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `cancel`: Resets an eligible pending credit.
- `detail`: Returns the selected record and associated state.
- `set_amount`: Assigns the waiver credit amount.
- `upload_waiver`: Stores the signed waiver and posts the credit.

Response: JSON success/error or message data, with operation-specific records or validation results. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

No gjc_csrf_verify call occurs in this handler.

##### POST /admin/api/maintenance_fees.php

Source: `admin/api/maintenance_fees.php`. Allowed role(s): finance. Collects all accrued rows for one student or all eligible students, creating a receipt per student and returning collection results. This operation does not debit a wallet.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `student_user_id`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `collect_all`: Collects accrued maintenance fees with a separate receipt per student.
- `collect_student`: Collects accrued maintenance fees for one student.

Response: JSON success/error or message data, with operation-specific records or validation results. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

No gjc_csrf_verify call occurs in this handler.

### 2.4 Account Provisioning and Enrollment

#### a. Module Description

The provisioning module administers user records, student imports, merchant bypass provisioning, product restrictions, school years, and enrollment status. Finance personnel operate the module, with additional super-administrator checks for selected destructive or privileged status changes.

#### b. Features

Signed CSV import. The maintenance page generates templates with a signed marker and exact expected columns, previews uploaded rows in the session, and imports validated student identities, courses, wallets, registry entries, and optional parents and links. Credential messages are queued. The unsigned sample CSV does not satisfy the current signed-template check.

Merchant bypass. The maintenance workflow can provision an owner, wallet, merchant record, and approved application through an explicit administrative action rather than a public application.

User restrictions. The user action endpoint suspends, bans, or lifts restrictions subject to target-role protections and reason requirements. Duration checks limit a timed suspension to the implemented maximum of 365 days.

School-year roster staging. The enrollment endpoint accepts CSV roster rows matched by school-issued student identifier, stages matched and unmatched records, previews differences, and applies statuses to the selected year. The available statuses are enrolled, not_enrolled, on_leave, dropped, transferred, and graduated.

Rollover and graduation. Year rollover records wallet-balance snapshots and carries enrollment data into the next period without issuing wallet value. Graduation and transferred status affect wallet eligibility; super-administrator operations support unmarking graduation and backfilling legacy year tags.

Student eligibility. Active enrollment permits normal access; unenrolled students receive a restricted read-only state, and exit states block the student dashboard path. The bootstrap behavior permits an active state when the enrollment structures or populated enrollment context are absent. An api enrollment source value exists, but an external registrar integration is [incomplete].

#### d. Database Tables Used

- **course**. Defines course or program records referenced by student_info. Key declared columns: `courseID`, `course_code`, `course_name`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **enrollment_roster_staging**. Stores parsed roster batches, school identifiers, matched student users, proposed status/year level, and processing state before application. Key declared columns: `id`, `school_year_id`, `status`, `batch_id`, `student_id_number`, `yr_lvl`, `matched_user_id`, `match_status`, `uploaded_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **fee_waiver_credits**. Stores one student's waiver amount, workflow state, uploaded document, and claim/administrative metadata. student_user_id identifies the credited student. Key declared columns: `id`, `student_user_id`, `amount`, `status`, `waiver_file`, `claimed_at`, `claimed_by_user_id`, `claim_reference`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **imported_student_registry**. Tracks imported school identifiers and provisioned user/profile/parent metadata to support administrative CSV processing. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `import_batch_id`, `student_id_number`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `course_program`, `email`, `phone_number`, `parent_name`, `parent_email`, `parent_contact`, `parent_user_id`, `parent_status`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **merchant**. Stores the historical/current merchant business identity and account/stall association used by compatibility access. Key declared columns: `userID`, `merchantID`, `stall_name`, `stall_id`, `operational_status`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `notes`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **merchant_inventory**. Stores merchant-owned SKU, product description, category, unit, price, stock, alert threshold, availability, and restriction fields. merchant_user_id identifies the owner. Key declared columns: `id`, `merchant_user_id`, `sku`, `product_name`, `description`, `category`, `unit`, `price`, `stock_qty`, `min_stock_alert`, `is_available`, `is_restricted`, `restriction_note`, `approved_by`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **merchant_wallets**. Stores the merchant owner's balance. user_id identifies users; purchase, settlement, and merchant-funded load movements reference its wallet id. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `balance`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **parent_student_links**. Relates a parent record to a student user and enforces link uniqueness. This association authorizes parent supervision and allowance or waiver operations. Key declared columns: `id`, `parent_id`, `student_user_id`, `linked_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **parent_wallets**. Stores each parent's independent balance. parent_id identifies parents; transactions and parent shopping records can reference its id. Key declared columns: `id`, `parent_id`, `balance`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **parents**. Stores the parent-to-user association and low-balance alert threshold. user_id identifies users; parent_student_links, parent_wallets, and parent_alerts use the parent id. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `low_balance_threshold`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **restricted_products**. Stores product-name restrictions, match type, category, reason, active state, and finance attribution. Key declared columns: `id`, `product_name`, `category`, `reason`, `match_type`, `is_active`, `flagged_by`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `calories`, `sugar_g`, `fat_g`, `protein_g`, `sodium_mg`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **role**. Defines the historical numeric role catalogue. users.roleID references the role identifier; application role normalization also recognizes newer identifiers and subroles. Key declared columns: `roleID`, `role_name`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **school_year_balances**. Stores student closing/carry-over balance snapshots per school year. Rollover records balances without changing wallet value. Key declared columns: `id`, `student_user_id`, `school_year_id`, `starting_balance`, `final_ending_balance`, `archived_at`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **school_years**. Defines named school-year intervals and the active-year flag. Enrollment, balance snapshots, and tagged transactions reference the year id. Key declared columns: `id`, `school_year_name`, `start_date`, `end_date`, `is_active`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **stall_applications**. Stores current public application identity, business/contact data, document paths, preferred/awarded stall, meeting, contract, deposit/advance, review status, and provisioning metadata. Key declared columns: `id`, `merchant_user_id`, `status`, `stall_id`, `business_name`, `first_name`, `middle_name`, `last_name`, `suffix`, `sex`, `street`, `barangay`, `city`, `province`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **stalls**. Stores the school stall identifier, map position, rental attributes, assignment, and occupancy/hold state. Key declared columns: `status`, `stall_id`, `label`, `row_label`, `col_number`, `area_sqm`, `monthly_rate`, `merchant_id`, `pending_expires_at`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **student_enrollments**. Stores explicit per-student, per-year enrollment status, year level, source, and administrative metadata. Student/year uniqueness prevents duplicate enrollment contexts. Key declared columns: `id`, `student_user_id`, `school_year_id`, `status`, `yr_lvl`, `source`, `enrolled_at`, `status_changed_at`, `changed_by`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **student_info**. Stores school-issued student identity, year level, course linkage, and graduation metadata for users. studentID is used for lookup and roster matching. Key declared columns: `userID`, `stud_infoID`, `studentID`, `yr_lvl`, `courseID`, `graduated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **student_wallets**. Stores the student user's balance, freeze flag, and spending controls. user_id identifies users; current transactions and peer transfers attribute movements to this wallet. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `balance`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `daily_spend_limit`, `is_frozen`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **transactions**. Stores the current referenced wallet ledger, including type, amount, status, fees, initiating user, wallet attribution, and school-year context. Optional student, merchant, and parent wallet identifiers distinguish the movement. Key declared columns: `id`, `student_wallet_id`, `merchant_wallet_id`, `transaction_type`, `amount`, `status`, `reference_no`, `initiated_by`, `voucher_id`, `vault_before`, `vault_after`, `total_in_circulation`, `notes`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **users**. Stores login identity, password hash, role/subrole, merchant ownership, profile, first-login flags, and account restrictions. userID is the principal identity referenced by wallets and role-specific records; roleID relates to role. Key declared columns: `userID`, `roleID`, `last_name`, `first_name`, `middle_name`, `suffix`, `contact_number`, `email`, `password`, `mint_pin`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **wallet**. Stores the historical generic wallet model. Active role-specific operations use student_wallets, merchant_wallets, and parent_wallets. Key declared columns: `userID`, `balance`, `wallet_id`, `last_updated`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.

#### e. API Endpoints and HTTP Entry Points

Routes are relative to the application base URL. The method notation identifies the request inputs consumed by the implementation; it does not imply a universal method-rejection guard. Where GET and POST are merged, both can supply an action. Each PHP file is counted once as an entry point; its action variants are listed separately.

##### POST /admin/api/restricted_products.php

Source: `admin/api/restricted_products.php`. Allowed role(s): finance. Creates, activates/deactivates, or deletes product rules and lifts the restricted-product suspension of a merchant. Rule input includes product_name, category, match_type, and reason.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `category`, `id`, `is_active`, `match_type`, `product_name`, `reason`, `user_id`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `delete_restriction`: Deletes a restriction rule.
- `flag_product`: Creates a product restriction rule.
- `lift_suspension`: Lifts the applicable suspension after authorization checks.
- `toggle_restriction`: Changes a restriction rule's active state.

Response: JSON success/error or message data; payload keys directly constructed include `success`, `message`, `existing_disabled`. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

No gjc_csrf_verify call occurs in this handler.

##### POST /admin/api/school_years.php

Source: `admin/api/school_years.php`. Allowed role(s): finance. Looks up a student; previews rollover; creates a year; stages a roster; previews and applies statuses; rolls over; marks one or a year's students graduated; reverses graduation; or backfills legacy tags. unmark_graduate and backfill_legacy have additional super-administrator checks.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `apply_all`, `batch_id`, `bulk_status`, `end_date`, `new_school_year_id`, `old_school_year_id`, `roster_csv`, `school_year_id`, `school_year_name`, `start_date`, `statuses`, `student_user_id`, `student_user_ids`, `yr_lvl`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `apply_statuses`: Applies selected staged enrollment statuses.
- `backfill_legacy`: Assigns school-year context to eligible legacy records.
- `create_year`: Creates an inactive school-year record.
- `mark_graduate`: Marks the selected student as graduated.
- `mark_graduate_bulk_year`: Marks the selected year's student group graduated.
- `preview_diff`: Returns staged roster and existing enrollment differences.
- `preview_rollover`: Returns proposed year-end rollover information.
- `rollover`: Records closing balances and changes the active school-year context.
- `student_lookup`: Returns identity, wallet, and enrollment information.
- `unmark_graduate`: Reverses the selected graduation state under elevated authorization.
- `upload_roster`: Parses and stages a registrar CSV roster.

Response: JSON success/error or message data, with operation-specific records or validation results. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

No gjc_csrf_verify call occurs in this handler.

##### POST /admin/api/users.php

Source: `admin/api/users.php`. Allowed role(s): finance. Suspends, bans, or lifts a user's restriction. Target-role protections, a reason, duration validation, and the ban confirmation distinguish the actions.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `confirm`, `duration`, `reason`, `user_id`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `ban`: Applies a permanent account ban.
- `lift_ban`: Clears an authorized account ban.
- `lift_suspension`: Lifts the applicable suspension after authorization checks.
- `suspend`: Applies a timed or indefinite account suspension.

Response: JSON success/error or message data, with operation-specific records or validation results. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

No gjc_csrf_verify call occurs in this handler.

Request fields read directly: `business_name`, `download_template`, `email`, `fee_waiver_csv`, `fee_waiver_import_action`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `merchant_business_name`, `merchant_bypass_action`, `merchant_email`, `merchant_first_name`, `merchant_last_name`, `merchant_middle_name`, `merchant_notes`, `merchant_phone`, `merchant_sex`, `merchant_stall_id`, `merchant_suffix`, `middle_name`, `phone`, `sex`, `stall_id`, `student_import_action`, `students_csv`, `suffix`, `temp_password`. ### 2.5 Stall Applications and Awarding

#### a. Module Description

The application module presents available school stalls and receives merchant applications. Applicants supply personal and business details and supporting files; finance personnel schedule verification and award a stall after the required contract and rental payments.

#### b. Features

Public stall map. StallManager returns a normalized ten-stall map across rows A and B and removes expired legacy pending holds. The current application's preferred stall is a preference rather than a guaranteed allocation.

Application staging. Five document categories cover a profile photograph, business permit, sanitary permit, clearance, and GJC requirements. A random session-associated draft token names staged uploads; successful submission moves the files to the application's directory, while opportunistic cleanup removes stale drafts after forty-eight hours.

Meeting allocation. Scheduling uses seven daily time slots at 09:00, 10:00, 11:00, 13:00, 14:00, 15:00, and 16:00, skips weekends and configured holidays, and serializes competing assignments with a database advisory lock. Meeting emails include the appointment and original-document instructions.

Review and award. Finance uploads a contract, records deposit and advance amounts and rental dates, and awards an available stall after the required two-month deposit and one-month advance are satisfied. Awarding creates the owner account, merchant, wallet, lease, and stall association and queues account credentials.

Application lifecycle. Review actions reject or reschedule applications, mark them viewed, and retrieve meeting availability. Overdue meetings can expire lazily as no-shows; archived rejection reactivation copies an application into the current pipeline. Historical approval states remain in migrations and are not treated as an additional current workflow.

#### d. Database Tables Used

- **archived_rejections**. Stores archived declined applications and reactivation metadata. Reactivation creates a current application rather than treating the archive as an active award. Key declared columns: `id`, `original_application_id`, `rejected_at_step`, `business_name`, `proprietor_name`, `contact_number`, `email`, `profile_picture`, `business_permit`, `sanitary_permit`, `gjc_requirements`, `clearance`, `rejection_reason`, `rejected_by`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **meeting_holidays**. Defines dates excluded from application meeting allocation. Key declared columns: `id`, `holiday_date`, `name`, `created_by`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **meeting_settings**. Stores meeting-location or scheduling configuration used by appointment helpers. Key declared columns: `id`, `default_location`, `down_payment_default_amount`, `updated_by`, `updated_at`, `wallet_inactivity_days`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **merchant**. Stores the historical/current merchant business identity and account/stall association used by compatibility access. Key declared columns: `userID`, `merchantID`, `stall_name`, `stall_id`, `operational_status`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `notes`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **merchant_accounts**. Stores the earlier merchant account representation retained in the historical schema. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `application_id`, `temp_password_plain`, `created_by`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **merchant_leases**. Stores merchant tenancy, stall number/name, monthly rent, deposit, start/end dates, status, notes, due date, and reminder period. merchant_user_id identifies the owner. Key declared columns: `id`, `merchant_user_id`, `status`, `stall_number`, `stall_name`, `monthly_rent`, `deposit_amount`, `lease_start`, `lease_end`, `next_due_date`, `contract_notes`, `created_by`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **merchant_wallets**. Stores the merchant owner's balance. user_id identifies users; purchase, settlement, and merchant-funded load movements reference its wallet id. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `balance`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **restricted_products**. Stores product-name restrictions, match type, category, reason, active state, and finance attribution. Key declared columns: `id`, `product_name`, `category`, `reason`, `match_type`, `is_active`, `flagged_by`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `calories`, `sugar_g`, `fat_g`, `protein_g`, `sodium_mg`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **stall_applications**. Stores current public application identity, business/contact data, document paths, preferred/awarded stall, meeting, contract, deposit/advance, review status, and provisioning metadata. Key declared columns: `id`, `merchant_user_id`, `status`, `stall_id`, `business_name`, `first_name`, `middle_name`, `last_name`, `suffix`, `sex`, `street`, `barangay`, `city`, `province`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **stalls**. Stores the school stall identifier, map position, rental attributes, assignment, and occupancy/hold state. Key declared columns: `status`, `stall_id`, `label`, `row_label`, `col_number`, `area_sqm`, `monthly_rate`, `merchant_id`, `pending_expires_at`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **users**. Stores login identity, password hash, role/subrole, merchant ownership, profile, first-login flags, and account restrictions. userID is the principal identity referenced by wallets and role-specific records; roleID relates to role. Key declared columns: `userID`, `roleID`, `last_name`, `first_name`, `middle_name`, `suffix`, `contact_number`, `email`, `password`, `mint_pin`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.

#### e. API Endpoints and HTTP Entry Points

Routes are relative to the application base URL. The method notation identifies the request inputs consumed by the implementation; it does not imply a universal method-rejection guard. Where GET and POST are merged, both can supply an action. Each PHP file is counted once as an entry point; its action variants are listed separately.

##### GET / POST /admin/api/archived_rejections.php

Source: `admin/api/archived_rejections.php`. Allowed role(s): finance. Lists unreactivated archived records or reactivates the selected id into a new application pipeline record.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `id`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `list`: Returns the scoped record collection.
- `reactivate`: Creates a current application from the selected archive.

Response: JSON success/error or message data, with operation-specific records or validation results. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

No gjc_csrf_verify call occurs in this handler.

##### POST /admin/api/stall_applications.php

Source: `admin/api/stall_applications.php`. Allowed role(s): finance. Uploads a signed contract, records rental deposit and advance, awards a selected stall, rejects an application, returns meeting slots, reschedules a meeting, or marks an application viewed. Award prerequisites are checked on the server.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `advance_amount`, `app_id`, `contract`, `date`, `deposit_amount`, `meeting_date`, `meeting_time`, `payment_schedule_day`, `reason`, `rental_start_date`, `stall_id`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `award`: Finalizes the application and provisions its merchant and tenancy records.
- `mark_viewed`: Stamps application review state.
- `meeting_slots`: Returns available times for the requested date.
- `record_payment`: Records the application deposit, advance, rental start, and schedule day.
- `reject`: Rejects the application and queues a notice.
- `reschedule_meeting`: Changes the appointment and queues a notice.
- `upload_contract`: Stores a validated signed contract.

Response: JSON success/error or message data, with operation-specific records or validation results. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

No gjc_csrf_verify call occurs in this handler.

##### GET /admin/stall_applications.php

Source: `admin/stall_applications.php`. Allowed role(s): finance. Presents pending and historical applications with contract, payment, meeting, and award controls.

Request: the current session and any shared-helper context; no direct named request field is read by this file.

Response: HTML page or redirect with validation/session feedback.

##### GET / POST /apply.php

Source: `apply.php`. Public; session state may affect redirection. Presents and processes the merchant application, staged documents, terms acceptance, and automatic meeting assignment.

Request fields read directly: `barangay`, `business_name`, `city`, `contact_number`, `email`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `middle_name`, `preferred_stall_id`, `province`, `sex`, `street`, `submitted`, `suffix`, `terms_accepted`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

Response: HTML page or redirect with validation/session feedback.

##### POST /apply_upload.php

Source: `apply_upload.php`. Public; session state may affect redirection. Stages one public application file selected by field and file, or clears the session's draft through action=clear. It returns staged-file metadata or validation failure.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `field`, `file`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `clear`: Clears the application's staged draft files.
- `upload`: Validates and stores the submitted image.

Response: JSON success/error or message data; payload keys directly constructed include `success`, `message`. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

No gjc_csrf_verify call occurs in this handler.

##### GET /stalls.php

Source: `stalls.php`. Public; session state may affect redirection. Displays the public normalized stall-availability map.

Request: the current session and any shared-helper context; no direct named request field is read by this file.

Response: HTML page or redirect with validation/session feedback.

### 2.6 Merchant Directory and Tenancy

#### a. Module Description

The tenancy module maintains the finance-facing merchant directory, lease terms, rental schedules, payment receipts, and owner document access. MerchantTenantDirectory supplies the common tenant model used by finance and merchant pages.

#### b. Features

Directory and lease presentation. Directory cards combine merchant identity, assigned stall, active lease, rent state, and review information. Finance detail views separate tenancy and compliance activity from merchant sales; merchant_card_views records the viewer's last inspection.

Rental accounting. The service divides a lease into monthly periods, clamps calendar arithmetic at month ends, allocates receipts to periods, computes balances and the next due date, and produces an account narrative. Lease end dates delimit the generated periods.

Payments and voiding. Finance records rental payments against a lease and period or voids an existing payment by deleting its receipt row. The schedule and due date are recomputed, and notifications record the resulting change.

Rent reminders. Finance rent-roll access and merchant dashboard access can dispatch a once-per-period reminder within the configured window, which defaults to seven days. This behavior is request-driven rather than a scheduled rent worker.

Document delivery. Merchant contract and document handlers check owner access and stream approved files. Finance lease and merchant-detail pages expose scoped records and paginated inventory, rental payments, or permitted activity.

#### d. Database Tables Used

- **merchant**. Stores the historical/current merchant business identity and account/stall association used by compatibility access. Key declared columns: `userID`, `merchantID`, `stall_name`, `stall_id`, `operational_status`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `notes`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **merchant_card_views**. Stores finance viewer/merchant inspection timestamps used for directory review indicators. Key declared columns: `merchant_id`, `last_viewed_at`, `viewed_by`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **merchant_documents**. Stores the owner's current compliance-document key, file path, original filename, media information, and update metadata. Key declared columns: `id`, `merchant_user_id`, `doc_key`, `file_path`, `original_name`, `uploaded_by`, `uploaded_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **merchant_inventory**. Stores merchant-owned SKU, product description, category, unit, price, stock, alert threshold, availability, and restriction fields. merchant_user_id identifies the owner. Key declared columns: `id`, `merchant_user_id`, `sku`, `product_name`, `description`, `category`, `unit`, `price`, `stock_qty`, `min_stock_alert`, `is_available`, `is_restricted`, `restriction_note`, `approved_by`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **merchant_leases**. Stores merchant tenancy, stall number/name, monthly rent, deposit, start/end dates, status, notes, due date, and reminder period. merchant_user_id identifies the owner. Key declared columns: `id`, `merchant_user_id`, `status`, `stall_number`, `stall_name`, `monthly_rent`, `deposit_amount`, `lease_start`, `lease_end`, `next_due_date`, `contract_notes`, `created_by`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **merchant_rent_payments**. Stores rental receipts by lease, period, amount, date, payment method, recorder, and notes. lease_id relates to merchant_leases. Key declared columns: `id`, `lease_id`, `amount_paid`, `period_covered`, `payment_date`, `payment_method`, `received_by`, `reference_no`, `notes`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **notifications**. Stores recipient-specific in-application notices, type/icon/title/body, target link, and read state. user_id identifies the recipient. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `type`, `icon`, `title`, `message`, `link`, `is_read`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **stall_applications**. Stores current public application identity, business/contact data, document paths, preferred/awarded stall, meeting, contract, deposit/advance, review status, and provisioning metadata. Key declared columns: `id`, `merchant_user_id`, `status`, `stall_id`, `business_name`, `first_name`, `middle_name`, `last_name`, `suffix`, `sex`, `street`, `barangay`, `city`, `province`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **stalls**. Stores the school stall identifier, map position, rental attributes, assignment, and occupancy/hold state. Key declared columns: `status`, `stall_id`, `label`, `row_label`, `col_number`, `area_sqm`, `monthly_rate`, `merchant_id`, `pending_expires_at`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **systemic_audit_trail**. Stores redacted actor/action/target events, old/new serialized values, request context, outcome, and chained hashes. User attribution is nullable for unknown or pre-authentication actors. Key declared columns: `user_id`, `log_id`, `user_role`, `action_type`, `stall_id`, `affected_table`, `old_value`, `new_value`, `ip_address`, `user_agent`, `timestamp`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **users**. Stores login identity, password hash, role/subrole, merchant ownership, profile, first-login flags, and account restrictions. userID is the principal identity referenced by wallets and role-specific records; roleID relates to role. Key declared columns: `userID`, `roleID`, `last_name`, `first_name`, `middle_name`, `suffix`, `contact_number`, `email`, `password`, `mint_pin`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.

#### e. API Endpoints and HTTP Entry Points

Routes are relative to the application base URL. The method notation identifies the request inputs consumed by the implementation; it does not imply a universal method-rejection guard. Where GET and POST are merged, both can supply an action. Each PHP file is counted once as an entry point; its action variants are listed separately.

##### GET / POST /admin/api/get_stall_details.php

Source: `admin/api/get_stall_details.php`. Authenticated finance context; explicit branch checks apply. Only toggle_product_restriction remains implemented. The request identifies item_id, restricted, and note; former modal read and lease actions are absent.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `item_id`, `note`, `restricted`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `toggle_product_restriction`: Changes the inventory restriction flag and note.

Response: JSON success/error or message data; payload keys directly constructed include `success`, `message`. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

No gjc_csrf_verify call occurs in this handler.

##### GET / POST /admin/api/leases.php

Source: `admin/api/leases.php`. Allowed role(s): finance. Returns a paginated rental ledger or eligible merchants, creates or updates a lease, records a period payment, or voids a payment. Record ownership is determined through the selected lease.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `amount_paid`, `contract_notes`, `deposit_amount`, `from`, `lease_end`, `lease_id`, `lease_start`, `merchant_user_id`, `monthly_rent`, `notes`, `page`, `payment_date`, `payment_id`, `payment_method`, `per_page`, `period_covered`, `stall_name`, `stall_number`, `status`, `to`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `create_lease`: Creates the tenant's lease terms.
- `get_ledger`: Returns the rental account and filtered payment page.
- `list_merchants`: Returns merchants available to the selector.
- `record_payment`: Records the module's payment fields.
- `update_lease`: Updates an existing lease and recomputes its schedule.
- `void_payment`: Deletes the selected rental receipt and recomputes the account.

Response: JSON success/error or message data; payload keys directly constructed include `success`, `message`, `merchants`, `lease`, `merchant`, `name`, `email`, `payments`, `id`, `ref`. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

No gjc_csrf_verify call occurs in this handler.

##### GET /admin/lease_details.php

Source: `admin/lease_details.php`. Allowed role(s): finance. Displays a signed lease account with schedule and paginated receipt details.

Request fields read directly: `all`, `page`, `ret`, `tab`, `token`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

Response: HTML page or redirect with validation/session feedback.

##### GET /admin/leases.php

Source: `admin/leases.php`. Allowed role(s): finance. Presents the searchable merchant directory and rent-roll views.

Request fields read directly: `page`, `q`, `view`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

Response: HTML page or redirect with validation/session feedback.

##### GET /admin/merchant_details.php

Source: `admin/merchant_details.php`. Allowed role(s): finance. Displays signed merchant tenancy, compliance, inventory, and permitted activity panels and records card inspection.

Request fields read directly: `apage`, `cat`, `ipage`, `q`, `restrict`, `tab`, `token`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

Response: HTML page or redirect with validation/session feedback.

##### GET /merchant/contract.php

Source: `merchant/contract.php`. Allowed role(s): merchant. Displays or downloads the awarded merchant contract.

Request fields read directly: `dl`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

Response: Inline document or attachment when dl requests downloading.

##### GET /merchant/doc.php

Source: `merchant/doc.php`. Allowed role(s): merchant. Merchant owner/staff checks further delimit access. Displays or downloads a selected owner compliance document.

Request fields read directly: `dl`, `t`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

Response: Inline document or attachment when dl requests downloading.

##### GET /merchant/rent.php

Source: `merchant/rent.php`. Allowed role(s): merchant. Merchant owner/staff checks further delimit access. Presents the owner's lease, period balances, and rental-payment history.

Request fields read directly: `all`, `page`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

Response: HTML page or redirect with validation/session feedback.

### 2.7 Merchant Operations

#### a. Module Description

The merchant module supports owner and staff sales operations, inventory, wallet loading, refunds, remittance reporting, profile maintenance, and owner administration. Merchant staff act against the resolved owner's resources within each endpoint's explicit role checks.

#### b. Features

Inventory. Owners and permitted staff manage SKU, name, description, category, unit price, stock, alert threshold, and availability. A merchant-scoped unique SKU index is created when compatible data permits it; restriction checks can reject products and record violations.

Point of sale. The POS endpoint validates inventory and totals, supports student lookup and direct student-wallet payment, decrements stock, records transactions, and accrues applicable maintenance fees. Pending queues combine POS QR orders and cart orders, with status, order-detail, and void operations.

QR order preparation. A QR order receives a random token, an eight-character short code, and a five-minute expiry. Student and parent validation endpoints resolve pending orders, but the former scan.php and pay_qr.php payment pages are absent; a complete token-order payment path is [incomplete]. Cart checkout uses a separate pending-cart and merchant-identification flow.

Returns. A return requires an eligible completed student-wallet payment and sufficient merchant value, creates a refund movement, marks the original transaction reversed, and voids eligible accrued maintenance fees. It does not establish a general parent-wallet or voucher refund facility.

Remittance reporting. Sales summaries distinguish remitted and unremitted reporting periods. Recording a remittance creates a report boundary rather than transferring wallet funds; report and backup routes supply owner-facing output.

Staff management. Owners create, update, deactivate, reset passwords for, or soft-remove staff accounts. Password resets set first-login/change flags; removal records staff_removed_at rather than deleting the user record.

Merchant identity and compliance. Settings and profile handlers update a stall name, logo, contact details, compliance documents, personal profile, and password. Owner-only routes present static merchant QR information, contracts, rent, and encashment requests. Notification endpoints operate on the signed-in user's notification rows.

Anonymous functions are identified by source line and, where available, JavaScript offset. Callback return values belong to the enclosing operation. SQL-table references below are direct references; shared service calls can use additional tables.
