#### d. Database Tables Used

- **auth_remember_tokens**. Stores persistent-login selectors, hashed validators, user attribution, and expiry. Raw validators are not stored as the verification value. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `selector`, `token_hash`, `expires_at`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **cart_orders**. Stores a buyer's pending/completed shop order, merchant, JSON items, total, reference, and wallet attribution. buyer_role and nullable student/parent fields distinguish student and parent purchases. Key declared columns: `id`, `student_user_id`, `merchant_user_id`, `student_wallet_id`, `merchant_wallet_id`, `parent_wallet_id`, `amount`, `status`, `reference_no`, `buyer_role`, `parent_user_id`, `description`, `items_json`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **encashment_requests**. Stores merchant cash-out requests, requested amounts, status, and release attribution. merchant_wallet_id identifies the wallet validated during release. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `merchant_wallet_id`, `amount`, `status`, `method`, `reference_no`, `released_by`, `released_at`, `rejected_by`, `rejected_at`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **maintenance_fees**. Stores assessed charges by student, transaction reference, amount, rate, and accrued/collected/void state. collection_id associates a collected charge with its receipt. Key declared columns: `id`, `student_user_id`, `school_year_id`, `status`, `reference_no`, `source_type`, `txn_amount`, `fee_amount`, `created_at`, `collected_at`, `collected_by`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **merchant**. Stores the historical/current merchant business identity and account/stall association used by compatibility access. Key declared columns: `userID`, `merchantID`, `stall_name`, `stall_id`, `operational_status`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `notes`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **merchant_documents**. Stores the owner's current compliance-document key, file path, original filename, media information, and update metadata. Key declared columns: `id`, `merchant_user_id`, `doc_key`, `file_path`, `original_name`, `uploaded_by`, `uploaded_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **merchant_inventory**. Stores merchant-owned SKU, product description, category, unit, price, stock, alert threshold, availability, and restriction fields. merchant_user_id identifies the owner. Key declared columns: `id`, `merchant_user_id`, `sku`, `product_name`, `description`, `category`, `unit`, `price`, `stock_qty`, `min_stock_alert`, `is_available`, `is_restricted`, `restriction_note`, `approved_by`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **merchant_leases**. Stores merchant tenancy, stall number/name, monthly rent, deposit, start/end dates, status, notes, due date, and reminder period. merchant_user_id identifies the owner. Key declared columns: `id`, `merchant_user_id`, `status`, `stall_number`, `stall_name`, `monthly_rent`, `deposit_amount`, `lease_start`, `lease_end`, `next_due_date`, `contract_notes`, `created_by`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **merchant_qr_orders**. Stores expiring POS order tokens, short codes, JSON item snapshots, amount, buyer/payment references, and lifecycle status. Merchant and optional wallet references identify participants. Key declared columns: `id`, `merchant_user_id`, `merchant_wallet_id`, `amount`, `status`, `token`, `short_code`, `description`, `items_json`, `expires_at`, `paid_by`, `paid_ref`, `paid_at`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **merchant_rent_payments**. Stores rental receipts by lease, period, amount, date, payment method, recorder, and notes. lease_id relates to merchant_leases. Key declared columns: `id`, `lease_id`, `amount_paid`, `period_covered`, `payment_date`, `payment_method`, `received_by`, `reference_no`, `notes`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **merchant_wallets**. Stores the merchant owner's balance. user_id identifies users; purchase, settlement, and merchant-funded load movements reference its wallet id. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `balance`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **notifications**. Stores recipient-specific in-application notices, type/icon/title/body, target link, and read state. user_id identifies the recipient. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `type`, `icon`, `title`, `message`, `link`, `is_read`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **parent_student_links**. Relates a parent record to a student user and enforces link uniqueness. This association authorizes parent supervision and allowance or waiver operations. Key declared columns: `id`, `parent_id`, `student_user_id`, `linked_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **parent_wallets**. Stores each parent's independent balance. parent_id identifies parents; transactions and parent shopping records can reference its id. Key declared columns: `id`, `parent_id`, `balance`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **parents**. Stores the parent-to-user association and low-balance alert threshold. user_id identifies users; parent_student_links, parent_wallets, and parent_alerts use the parent id. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `low_balance_threshold`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **sales_remittances**. Stores merchant sales-report boundaries and aggregate remittance metadata. A row records reporting state rather than a wallet transfer. Key declared columns: `id`, `merchant_user_id`, `merchant_wallet_id`, `amount`, `staff_user_id`, `reference_no`, `txn_count`, `period_start`, `period_end`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **stall_applications**. Stores current public application identity, business/contact data, document paths, preferred/awarded stall, meeting, contract, deposit/advance, review status, and provisioning metadata. Key declared columns: `id`, `merchant_user_id`, `status`, `stall_id`, `business_name`, `first_name`, `middle_name`, `last_name`, `suffix`, `sex`, `street`, `barangay`, `city`, `province`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **stalls**. Stores the school stall identifier, map position, rental attributes, assignment, and occupancy/hold state. Key declared columns: `status`, `stall_id`, `label`, `row_label`, `col_number`, `area_sqm`, `monthly_rate`, `merchant_id`, `pending_expires_at`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **student_info**. Stores school-issued student identity, year level, course linkage, and graduation metadata for users. studentID is used for lookup and roster matching. Key declared columns: `userID`, `stud_infoID`, `studentID`, `yr_lvl`, `courseID`, `graduated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **student_wallets**. Stores the student user's balance, freeze flag, and spending controls. user_id identifies users; current transactions and peer transfers attribute movements to this wallet. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `balance`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `daily_spend_limit`, `is_frozen`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **system_settings**. Stores authorized circulation cap, cashier vault value, and related system controls. CirculationEngine serializes value-changing operations by locking its settings row. Key declared columns: `id`, `total_circulation_cap`, `cashier_vault_points`, `last_cap_increased_by`, `last_cap_increased_at`, `updated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **systemic_audit_trail**. Stores redacted actor/action/target events, old/new serialized values, request context, outcome, and chained hashes. User attribution is nullable for unknown or pre-authentication actors. Key declared columns: `user_id`, `log_id`, `user_role`, `action_type`, `stall_id`, `affected_table`, `old_value`, `new_value`, `ip_address`, `user_agent`, `timestamp`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **transactions**. Stores the current referenced wallet ledger, including type, amount, status, fees, initiating user, wallet attribution, and school-year context. Optional student, merchant, and parent wallet identifiers distinguish the movement. Key declared columns: `id`, `student_wallet_id`, `merchant_wallet_id`, `transaction_type`, `amount`, `status`, `reference_no`, `initiated_by`, `voucher_id`, `vault_before`, `vault_after`, `total_in_circulation`, `notes`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **users**. Stores login identity, password hash, role/subrole, merchant ownership, profile, first-login flags, and account restrictions. userID is the principal identity referenced by wallets and role-specific records; roleID relates to role. Key declared columns: `userID`, `roleID`, `last_name`, `first_name`, `middle_name`, `suffix`, `contact_number`, `email`, `password`, `mint_pin`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **vouchers**. Stores historical issued voucher value, validity, ownership, and status. Eligible active voucher value remains in circulation accounting. Key declared columns: `id`, `status`, `qr_code_hash`, `voucher_code`, `issued_by`, `is_refundable`, `visitor_name`, `visitor_contact`, `initial_value`, `original_amount`, `remaining_balance`, `expired_at`, `cancelled_at`, `last_used_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.

#### e. API Endpoints and HTTP Entry Points

Routes are relative to the application base URL. The method notation identifies the request inputs consumed by the implementation; it does not imply a universal method-rejection guard. Where GET and POST are merged, both can supply an action. Each PHP file is counted once as an entry point; its action variants are listed separately.

##### POST /merchant/api/business_profile.php

Source: `merchant/api/business_profile.php`. Allowed role(s): merchant. Merchant owner/staff checks further delimit access. Owner-only actions upload_document and update_contact replace a compliance file or update business contact information. The handler explicitly requires POST and verifies CSRF.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `contact_number`, `csrf_token`, `doc_key`, `file`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `update_contact`: Updates validated business contact fields.
- `upload_document`: Replaces the selected compliance document.

Response: JSON success/error or message data, with operation-specific records or validation results. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

CSRF verification occurs in this file; branch-specific scope applies where described above.

##### POST /merchant/api/inventory.php

Source: `merchant/api/inventory.php`. Allowed role(s): merchant. add_product, edit_product, and delete_product require an owner or permitted legacy merchant. update_stock permits the staff workflow and scopes the item to the resolved merchant owner.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `category`, `description`, `is_available`, `item_id`, `min_stock_alert`, `price`, `product_name`, `sku`, `stock_qty`, `unit`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `add_product`: Creates an owned inventory item.
- `delete_product`: Deletes an eligible owned item.
- `edit_product`: Updates an owned inventory item.
- `update_stock`: Updates the owned item's stock quantity.

Response: JSON success/error or message data; payload keys directly constructed include `success`, `message`, `blocked`, `attempted_name`, `reason`, `violation_count`, `warn_at`, `risk_at`, `suspend_days`, `suspended_until`, `is_restricted`. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

No gjc_csrf_verify call occurs in this handler.

##### GET / POST /merchant/api/notifications.php

Source: `merchant/api/notifications.php`. Allowed role(s): merchant. Lists the current merchant user's notifications, counts unread rows, or marks a selected/all notification read. mark_read requires POST and CSRF. The endpoint's merchant guard does not itself prohibit staff.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `id`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `list`: Returns the scoped record collection.
- `mark_read`: Marks scoped notification or alert rows read.
- `unread_count`: Returns the scoped unread count.

Response: JSON success/error or message data; payload keys directly constructed include `success`, `unread_count`, `notifications`, `id`, `type`, `icon`, `title`, `message`, `link`, `is_read`, `created_at`. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

CSRF verification occurs in this file; branch-specific scope applies where described above.

##### POST /merchant/api/pos.php

Source: `merchant/api/pos.php`. Allowed role(s): merchant. Creates expiring QR orders, checks status, retrieves the pending queue or order detail, voids an eligible order, looks up a student, processes direct POS payment, summarizes sales, and records a remittance reporting period. create_qr_order verifies CSRF; the other actions use their own branch checks.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `items`, `order_id`, `source`, `student_id`, `total`, `wallet_id`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `check_order_status`: Returns the QR order's current state.
- `create_qr_order`: Validates items and creates a short-lived QR order.
- `get_sales_summary`: Returns merchant sales aggregates.
- `get_today_sales`: Returns the current day's merchant sales.
- `list_queue`: Returns pending POS and cart orders.
- `lookup_student`: Returns the matching student and wallet.
- `process_pos`: Charges the selected student's wallet for validated POS items.
- `remit_sales`: Records a sales remittance report boundary without moving money.
- `view_order`: Returns scoped POS or cart detail.
- `void_order`: Voids an eligible scoped order.

Response: JSON success/error or message data; payload keys directly constructed include `success`, `message`, `order_id`, `qr_payload`, `short_code`, `summary`, `expires_at`, `status`, `paid_ref`, `paid_at`, `orders`, `todays_sales`, `pending_amount`, `total_earned`, `last_remit`, `sales`, `reference_no`, `amount`, `txn_count`, `time`, `report_url`, `reference`, `description`, `items`, `created_at`, `student_name`, `type`, `merchant_wallet_id`, `merchant_user_id`, `merchant`, `wallet_qr_url`, `name`, `user_id`, `wallet_id`, `balance`, `total`. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

CSRF verification occurs in this file; branch-specific scope applies where described above.

##### POST /merchant/api/profile.php

Source: `merchant/api/profile.php`. Allowed role(s): merchant. Merchant owner/staff checks further delimit access. Updates the owner's stall display name or uploads/removes its logo. Image validation and owner checks determine the accepted change.

Request fields read directly: `logo`, `remove_logo`, `stall_name`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

Response: JSON success/error or message data; payload keys directly constructed include `success`, `message`, `stall_name`, `logo_url`. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

No gjc_csrf_verify call occurs in this handler.

##### POST /merchant/api/returns.php

Source: `merchant/api/returns.php`. Allowed role(s): merchant. issue_return identifies an eligible transaction and refund reason, transfers merchant value back to the student, reverses the original ledger status, and returns refund data.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `notes`, `reason`, `transaction_id`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `issue_return`: Reverses an eligible student purchase with a new refund movement.

Response: JSON success/error or message data; payload keys directly constructed include `success`, `message`, `reference`. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

No gjc_csrf_verify call occurs in this handler.

##### POST /merchant/api/staff.php

Source: `merchant/api/staff.php`. Allowed role(s): merchant. Merchant owner/staff checks further delimit access. Owner-only creation, status toggle, update, password reset, and soft removal operate on linked staff. update_staff, reset_staff_password, and remove_staff verify CSRF; creation and status toggle do not.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `contact_number`, `email`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `middle_name`, `password`, `position`, `suffix`, `user_id`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `create_staff`: Creates a linked staff account.
- `remove_staff`: Soft-removes a linked staff account.
- `reset_staff_password`: Sets a new password and forces password change.
- `toggle_staff_status`: Changes a linked staff account's active state.
- `update_staff`: Updates a linked staff profile.

Response: JSON success/error or message data; payload keys directly constructed include `success`, `message`, `user_id`, `new_status`. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

CSRF verification occurs in this file; branch-specific scope applies where described above.

##### GET / POST /merchant/api/topup.php

Source: `merchant/api/topup.php`. Allowed role(s): merchant. Looks up a student or their linked parent and loads the selected wallet from the merchant owner's wallet. The request uses cash_amount and the applicable recipient identifier.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `cash_amount`, `parent_id`, `school_id`, `student_wallet_id`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `load_parent_wallet`: Loads a parent from merchant funds.
- `load_wallet`: Loads a student from merchant funds.
- `lookup_parent_by_student`: Resolves the student's linked parent and wallet.
- `lookup_student`: Returns the matching student and wallet.

Response: JSON success/error or message data; payload keys directly constructed include `success`, `name`, `user_id`, `wallet_id`, `parents`, `parent_id`, `error`. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

No gjc_csrf_verify call occurs in this handler.

### 2.8 Student Wallet and Shopping

#### a. Module Description

The student module presents the student's balance, activity, profile, notifications, fee-waiver state, transfers, and cart purchases. Shared enrollment and lockout rules restrict financial operations and determine which pages remain available.

#### b. Features

Wallet and history. Dashboard and summary handlers expose balance, recent transactions, account state, and notification counts. History supports school-year context; transaction details resolve signed references and verify ownership.

Cart preparation. Session cart entries contain item identifiers and quantities and are restricted to one merchant. Item-code entry and camera QR decoding populate the cart; submission revalidates the snapshot and creates a pending order without moving funds.

Checkout. The payment endpoint verifies CSRF, locks the student's pending order, matches the merchant, rechecks inventory and eligibility, enforces freeze and spending limits, transfers value, decrements stock, marks the cart paid, and records notifications and applicable fees.

Peer transfer. The transfer endpoint looks up a recipient by school-issued identifier and, after CSRF and eligibility checks, transfers a positive permitted amount from the current student. Default settings impose a minimum amount of one and a daily transfer limit of 5,000, subject to the configured values and wallet controls.

Profile and credit claim. Students edit supported personal fields and passwords, inspect fees, and claim a posted waiver once. The wallet, settings, and transactions compatibility pages redirect to their current destinations. QR validation returns order information and does not itself settle a purchase.

#### d. Database Tables Used

- **cart_orders**. Stores a buyer's pending/completed shop order, merchant, JSON items, total, reference, and wallet attribution. buyer_role and nullable student/parent fields distinguish student and parent purchases. Key declared columns: `id`, `student_user_id`, `merchant_user_id`, `student_wallet_id`, `merchant_wallet_id`, `parent_wallet_id`, `amount`, `status`, `reference_no`, `buyer_role`, `parent_user_id`, `description`, `items_json`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **fee_waiver_credits**. Stores one student's waiver amount, workflow state, uploaded document, and claim/administrative metadata. student_user_id identifies the credited student. Key declared columns: `id`, `student_user_id`, `amount`, `status`, `waiver_file`, `claimed_at`, `claimed_by_user_id`, `claim_reference`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **maintenance_fees**. Stores assessed charges by student, transaction reference, amount, rate, and accrued/collected/void state. collection_id associates a collected charge with its receipt. Key declared columns: `id`, `student_user_id`, `school_year_id`, `status`, `reference_no`, `source_type`, `txn_amount`, `fee_amount`, `created_at`, `collected_at`, `collected_by`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **merchant_inventory**. Stores merchant-owned SKU, product description, category, unit, price, stock, alert threshold, availability, and restriction fields. merchant_user_id identifies the owner. Key declared columns: `id`, `merchant_user_id`, `sku`, `product_name`, `description`, `category`, `unit`, `price`, `stock_qty`, `min_stock_alert`, `is_available`, `is_restricted`, `restriction_note`, `approved_by`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **merchant_qr_orders**. Stores expiring POS order tokens, short codes, JSON item snapshots, amount, buyer/payment references, and lifecycle status. Merchant and optional wallet references identify participants. Key declared columns: `id`, `merchant_user_id`, `merchant_wallet_id`, `amount`, `status`, `token`, `short_code`, `description`, `items_json`, `expires_at`, `paid_by`, `paid_ref`, `paid_at`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **merchant_wallets**. Stores the merchant owner's balance. user_id identifies users; purchase, settlement, and merchant-funded load movements reference its wallet id. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `balance`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **notifications**. Stores recipient-specific in-application notices, type/icon/title/body, target link, and read state. user_id identifies the recipient. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `type`, `icon`, `title`, `message`, `link`, `is_read`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **p2p_transfers**. Stores peer-transfer attribution, amount, message/reference, and timing in association with student wallets or users and the transaction ledger. Key declared columns: `id`, `amount`, `status`, `reference_no`, `from_wallet_id`, `to_wallet_id`, `from_user_id`, `to_user_id`, `message`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **parent_student_links**. Relates a parent record to a student user and enforces link uniqueness. This association authorizes parent supervision and allowance or waiver operations. Key declared columns: `id`, `parent_id`, `student_user_id`, `linked_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **parents**. Stores the parent-to-user association and low-balance alert threshold. user_id identifies users; parent_student_links, parent_wallets, and parent_alerts use the parent id. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `low_balance_threshold`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **school_years**. Defines named school-year intervals and the active-year flag. Enrollment, balance snapshots, and tagged transactions reference the year id. Key declared columns: `id`, `school_year_name`, `start_date`, `end_date`, `is_active`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **student_enrollments**. Stores explicit per-student, per-year enrollment status, year level, source, and administrative metadata. Student/year uniqueness prevents duplicate enrollment contexts. Key declared columns: `id`, `student_user_id`, `school_year_id`, `status`, `yr_lvl`, `source`, `enrolled_at`, `status_changed_at`, `changed_by`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **student_info**. Stores school-issued student identity, year level, course linkage, and graduation metadata for users. studentID is used for lookup and roster matching. Key declared columns: `userID`, `stud_infoID`, `studentID`, `yr_lvl`, `courseID`, `graduated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **student_wallets**. Stores the student user's balance, freeze flag, and spending controls. user_id identifies users; current transactions and peer transfers attribute movements to this wallet. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `balance`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `daily_spend_limit`, `is_frozen`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **system_settings**. Stores authorized circulation cap, cashier vault value, and related system controls. CirculationEngine serializes value-changing operations by locking its settings row. Key declared columns: `id`, `total_circulation_cap`, `cashier_vault_points`, `last_cap_increased_by`, `last_cap_increased_at`, `updated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **topup_requests**. Stores operational student top-up request state and request attribution; its existence does not establish a current self-service request interface. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `student_wallet_id`, `amount`, `status`, `payment_method`, `reference_no`, `approved_by`, `approved_at`, `rejected_by`, `rejected_at`, `created_at`, `top_up_source`, `fee_amount`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **transactions**. Stores the current referenced wallet ledger, including type, amount, status, fees, initiating user, wallet attribution, and school-year context. Optional student, merchant, and parent wallet identifiers distinguish the movement. Key declared columns: `id`, `student_wallet_id`, `merchant_wallet_id`, `transaction_type`, `amount`, `status`, `reference_no`, `initiated_by`, `voucher_id`, `vault_before`, `vault_after`, `total_in_circulation`, `notes`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **users**. Stores login identity, password hash, role/subrole, merchant ownership, profile, first-login flags, and account restrictions. userID is the principal identity referenced by wallets and role-specific records; roleID relates to role. Key declared columns: `userID`, `roleID`, `last_name`, `first_name`, `middle_name`, `suffix`, `contact_number`, `email`, `password`, `mint_pin`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **vouchers**. Stores historical issued voucher value, validity, ownership, and status. Eligible active voucher value remains in circulation accounting. Key declared columns: `id`, `status`, `qr_code_hash`, `voucher_code`, `issued_by`, `is_refundable`, `visitor_name`, `visitor_contact`, `initial_value`, `original_amount`, `remaining_balance`, `expired_at`, `cancelled_at`, `last_used_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.

#### e. API Endpoints and HTTP Entry Points

Routes are relative to the application base URL. The method notation identifies the request inputs consumed by the implementation; it does not imply a universal method-rejection guard. Where GET and POST are merged, both can supply an action. Each PHP file is counted once as an entry point; its action variants are listed separately.

##### POST /student/api/cart.php

Source: `student/api/cart.php`. Allowed role(s): student. Maintains the student session cart, creates or retrieves a pending order, and cancels that order. Submission records an order without charging the wallet.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `code`, `item_id`, `qty`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `add_item`: Adds the item identified by code to the single-merchant cart.
- `cancel_my_order`: Cancels the current buyer's pending order.
- `clear_cart`: Clears the session cart.
- `get_cart`: Returns a revalidated session-cart snapshot.
- `get_pending_order`: Returns the current buyer's pending order.
- `remove_item`: Removes a cart item.
- `submit_order`: Creates a pending order from the current cart.
- `update_qty`: Changes an item quantity.

Response: JSON success/error or message data; payload keys directly constructed include `success`, `message`, `blocked`, `order`, `reference`, `merchant_user_id`, `merchant_label`, `lines`, `total`, `status`. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

No gjc_csrf_verify call occurs in this handler.

##### POST /student/api/checkout.php

Source: `student/api/checkout.php`. Allowed role(s): student. action=pay_order and merchant_user_id identify the checkout operation; the actual items and amount come from the current student's locked pending cart. CSRF and wallet eligibility checks precede payment.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `merchant_user_id`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `pay_order`: Charges the pending order and completes checkout.

Response: JSON success/error or message data; payload keys directly constructed include `success`, `code`, `message`, `reference`, `total`. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

CSRF verification occurs in this file; branch-specific scope applies where described above.

##### GET / POST /student/api/fee_waiver_claim.php

Source: `student/api/fee_waiver_claim.php`. Allowed role(s): student. action=claim verifies CSRF and claims the current student's posted waiver through the shared atomic claim helper.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `csrf_token`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `claim`: Claims the posted credit once into the student wallet.

Response: JSON success/error or message data; payload keys directly constructed include `success`, `error`, `message`, `reference`. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

CSRF verification occurs in this file; branch-specific scope applies where described above.

##### GET / POST /student/api/notifications.php

Source: `student/api/notifications.php`. Allowed role(s): student. Lists current-user notifications, returns the unread count, or marks rows read. mark_read explicitly requires POST and CSRF.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `id`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `list`: Returns the scoped record collection.
- `mark_read`: Marks scoped notification or alert rows read.
- `unread_count`: Returns the scoped unread count.

Response: JSON success/error or message data; payload keys directly constructed include `success`, `unread_count`, `notifications`, `id`, `type`, `icon`, `title`, `message`, `link`, `is_read`, `created_at`. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

CSRF verification occurs in this file; branch-specific scope applies where described above.

##### POST /student/api/transfer.php

Source: `student/api/transfer.php`. Allowed role(s): student. lookup uses student_id to resolve a recipient; transfer uses recipient_student_id, amount, and optional message to perform a guarded peer movement. Both branches require CSRF.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `amount`, `message`, `recipient_student_id`, `student_id`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `lookup`: Returns the peer-transfer recipient.
- `transfer`: Transfers value to the eligible recipient student.

Response: JSON success/error or message data; payload keys directly constructed include `success`, `code`, `message`, `name`, `user_id`, `reference`. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

CSRF verification occurs in this file; branch-specific scope applies where described above.

Response: JSON success/error or message data; payload keys directly constructed include `success`, `code`, `message`, `token`, `merchant`, `description`, `amount`, `expires_at`, `seconds_left`. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

CSRF verification occurs in this file; branch-specific scope applies where described above.

### 2.9 Parent Wallet and Supervision

#### a. Module Description

The parent module combines a parent's independent purchasing wallet with supervision of explicitly linked students. Parent-to-student links delimit access to activity, controls, allowance transfers, and waiver claims.

#### b. Features

Linking and oversight. Parents link a student by school identifier or remove an existing link. Linked-student pages present activity, fees, and wallet state; controls set wallet freezing, daily spending limits, and low-balance alert thresholds.

Allowance transfer. A parent sends value from the parent's wallet to a linked student's wallet after CSRF, ownership, balance, and eligibility validation. The transfer is an immediate internal movement without an extra allowance service fee; no recurring allowance scheduler is implemented.

Parent shopping. The parent cart and checkout handlers maintain the parent's pending order and charge the parent wallet after inventory and merchant checks. This purchase path uses the parent's funds rather than a linked student's balance.

Alerts and claims. Parent alerts identify linked-student balance conditions and support read marking. A parent can claim an eligible posted waiver for a linked student; the resulting credit belongs to the student.

Profile. The profile page updates supported identity fields and the password after its password validation. Parent transaction and activity pages restrict results to the parent or the verified link context.

#### d. Database Tables Used

- **cart_orders**. Stores a buyer's pending/completed shop order, merchant, JSON items, total, reference, and wallet attribution. buyer_role and nullable student/parent fields distinguish student and parent purchases. Key declared columns: `id`, `student_user_id`, `merchant_user_id`, `student_wallet_id`, `merchant_wallet_id`, `parent_wallet_id`, `amount`, `status`, `reference_no`, `buyer_role`, `parent_user_id`, `description`, `items_json`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **fee_waiver_credits**. Stores one student's waiver amount, workflow state, uploaded document, and claim/administrative metadata. student_user_id identifies the credited student. Key declared columns: `id`, `student_user_id`, `amount`, `status`, `waiver_file`, `claimed_at`, `claimed_by_user_id`, `claim_reference`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **merchant_inventory**. Stores merchant-owned SKU, product description, category, unit, price, stock, alert threshold, availability, and restriction fields. merchant_user_id identifies the owner. Key declared columns: `id`, `merchant_user_id`, `sku`, `product_name`, `description`, `category`, `unit`, `price`, `stock_qty`, `min_stock_alert`, `is_available`, `is_restricted`, `restriction_note`, `approved_by`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **merchant_qr_orders**. Stores expiring POS order tokens, short codes, JSON item snapshots, amount, buyer/payment references, and lifecycle status. Merchant and optional wallet references identify participants. Key declared columns: `id`, `merchant_user_id`, `merchant_wallet_id`, `amount`, `status`, `token`, `short_code`, `description`, `items_json`, `expires_at`, `paid_by`, `paid_ref`, `paid_at`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **merchant_wallets**. Stores the merchant owner's balance. user_id identifies users; purchase, settlement, and merchant-funded load movements reference its wallet id. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `balance`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **parent_alerts**. Stores parent-facing student balance alerts and read state. parent_id and student_user_id identify the relevant parent and student. Key declared columns: `id`, `parent_id`, `student_user_id`, `student_wallet_id`, `balance_at_alert`, `threshold`, `is_read`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **parent_student_links**. Relates a parent record to a student user and enforces link uniqueness. This association authorizes parent supervision and allowance or waiver operations. Key declared columns: `id`, `parent_id`, `student_user_id`, `linked_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **parent_wallets**. Stores each parent's independent balance. parent_id identifies parents; transactions and parent shopping records can reference its id. Key declared columns: `id`, `parent_id`, `balance`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **parents**. Stores the parent-to-user association and low-balance alert threshold. user_id identifies users; parent_student_links, parent_wallets, and parent_alerts use the parent id. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `low_balance_threshold`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **school_year_balances**. Stores student closing/carry-over balance snapshots per school year. Rollover records balances without changing wallet value. Key declared columns: `id`, `student_user_id`, `school_year_id`, `starting_balance`, `final_ending_balance`, `archived_at`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **school_years**. Defines named school-year intervals and the active-year flag. Enrollment, balance snapshots, and tagged transactions reference the year id. Key declared columns: `id`, `school_year_name`, `start_date`, `end_date`, `is_active`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **student_info**. Stores school-issued student identity, year level, course linkage, and graduation metadata for users. studentID is used for lookup and roster matching. Key declared columns: `userID`, `stud_infoID`, `studentID`, `yr_lvl`, `courseID`, `graduated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **student_wallets**. Stores the student user's balance, freeze flag, and spending controls. user_id identifies users; current transactions and peer transfers attribute movements to this wallet. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `balance`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `daily_spend_limit`, `is_frozen`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **system_settings**. Stores authorized circulation cap, cashier vault value, and related system controls. CirculationEngine serializes value-changing operations by locking its settings row. Key declared columns: `id`, `total_circulation_cap`, `cashier_vault_points`, `last_cap_increased_by`, `last_cap_increased_at`, `updated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **transactions**. Stores the current referenced wallet ledger, including type, amount, status, fees, initiating user, wallet attribution, and school-year context. Optional student, merchant, and parent wallet identifiers distinguish the movement. Key declared columns: `id`, `student_wallet_id`, `merchant_wallet_id`, `transaction_type`, `amount`, `status`, `reference_no`, `initiated_by`, `voucher_id`, `vault_before`, `vault_after`, `total_in_circulation`, `notes`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **users**. Stores login identity, password hash, role/subrole, merchant ownership, profile, first-login flags, and account restrictions. userID is the principal identity referenced by wallets and role-specific records; roleID relates to role. Key declared columns: `userID`, `roleID`, `last_name`, `first_name`, `middle_name`, `suffix`, `contact_number`, `email`, `password`, `mint_pin`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **vouchers**. Stores historical issued voucher value, validity, ownership, and status. Eligible active voucher value remains in circulation accounting. Key declared columns: `id`, `status`, `qr_code_hash`, `voucher_code`, `issued_by`, `is_refundable`, `visitor_name`, `visitor_contact`, `initial_value`, `original_amount`, `remaining_balance`, `expired_at`, `cancelled_at`, `last_used_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.

#### e. API Endpoints and HTTP Entry Points

Routes are relative to the application base URL. The method notation identifies the request inputs consumed by the implementation; it does not imply a universal method-rejection guard. Where GET and POST are merged, both can supply an action. Each PHP file is counted once as an entry point; its action variants are listed separately.

##### GET /parent/activity.php

Source: `parent/activity.php`. Allowed role(s): parent. Displays linked-student activity filtered by student, date interval, and type.

Request fields read directly: `from`, `student`, `to`, `type`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

Response: HTML page or redirect with validation/session feedback.

##### GET /parent/allowance.php

Source: `parent/allowance.php`. Allowed role(s): parent. Presents immediate allowance-transfer controls for linked students.

Request: the current session and any shared-helper context; no direct named request field is read by this file.

Response: HTML page or redirect with validation/session feedback.

##### GET / POST /parent/api/alerts.php

Source: `parent/api/alerts.php`. Allowed role(s): parent. The default get_alerts operation returns the parent's alerts; mark_read updates read state.

Request fields read directly: `action`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `get_alerts`: Returns the parent's alert list.
- `mark_read`: Marks scoped notification or alert rows read.

Response: JSON success/error or message data; payload keys directly constructed include `success`, `error`, `unread_count`, `alerts`. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

No gjc_csrf_verify call occurs in this handler.

##### GET / POST /parent/api/allowance.php

Source: `parent/api/allowance.php`. Allowed role(s): parent. action=send accepts student_user_id, amount, note, and csrf_token, verifies the parent–student link, and transfers the parent's wallet value to the student.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `amount`, `csrf_token`, `note`, `student_user_id`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `send`: Transfers an allowance to a linked student.

Response: JSON success/error or message data; payload keys directly constructed include `success`, `error`, `message`, `reference`. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

CSRF verification occurs in this file; branch-specific scope applies where described above.

##### POST /parent/api/cart.php

Source: `parent/api/cart.php`. Allowed role(s): parent. Maintains the parent session cart, creates or retrieves a pending order, and cancels that order. Submission records an order without charging the wallet.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `code`, `item_id`, `qty`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `add_item`: Adds the item identified by code to the single-merchant cart.
- `cancel_my_order`: Cancels the current buyer's pending order.
- `clear_cart`: Clears the session cart.
- `get_cart`: Returns a revalidated session-cart snapshot.
- `get_pending_order`: Returns the current buyer's pending order.
- `remove_item`: Removes a cart item.
- `submit_order`: Creates a pending order from the current cart.
- `update_qty`: Changes an item quantity.

Response: JSON success/error or message data; payload keys directly constructed include `success`, `message`, `blocked`, `order`, `reference`, `merchant_user_id`, `merchant_label`, `lines`, `total`, `status`. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

No gjc_csrf_verify call occurs in this handler.

##### POST /parent/api/checkout.php

Source: `parent/api/checkout.php`. Allowed role(s): parent. action=pay_order and merchant_user_id identify the checkout operation; the current parent's pending cart supplies the amount and items. CSRF and parent-wallet checks precede payment.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `merchant_user_id`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `pay_order`: Charges the pending order and completes checkout.

Response: JSON success/error or message data; payload keys directly constructed include `success`, `code`, `message`, `reference`, `total`. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

CSRF verification occurs in this file; branch-specific scope applies where described above.

##### GET / POST /parent/api/controls.php

Source: `parent/api/controls.php`. Allowed role(s): parent. Updates a linked student's freeze or daily limit, changes the parent's alert threshold, marks alerts read, or removes a student link.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `amount`, `student_user_id`, `value`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `mark_alerts_read`: Marks the parent's alert records read.
- `set_alert_threshold`: Changes the parent's low-balance alert threshold.
- `set_daily_limit`: Changes the linked student's spending limit.
- `set_frozen`: Changes the linked student's wallet freeze flag.
- `unlink_student`: Deletes the selected parent–student link.

Response: JSON success/error or message data; payload keys directly constructed include `success`, `error`. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

No gjc_csrf_verify call occurs in this handler.

##### GET / POST /parent/api/fee_waiver_claim.php

Source: `parent/api/fee_waiver_claim.php`. Allowed role(s): parent. action=claim requires CSRF and student_user_id for a verified linked student; the minted credit enters that student's wallet.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `csrf_token`, `student_user_id`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `claim`: Claims the posted credit once into the student wallet.

Response: JSON success/error or message data; payload keys directly constructed include `success`, `error`, `message`, `reference`. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

CSRF verification occurs in this file; branch-specific scope applies where described above.

##### GET / POST /parent/api/link.php

Source: `parent/api/link.php`. Allowed role(s): parent. Links by school_id or unlinks by student_user_id after student-role and parent-record checks.

Request fields read directly: `action`, `school_id`, `student_user_id`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

- `link_student`: Creates a link to the school-identifier-matched student.
- `unlink_student`: Deletes the selected parent–student link.

Response: JSON success/error or message data; payload keys directly constructed include `success`, `error`, `message`. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

No gjc_csrf_verify call occurs in this handler.

##### POST /parent/api/validate_qr.php

Source: `parent/api/validate_qr.php`. Signed-in parent. Resolves token or code for a pending, unexpired merchant QR order after parent-session and CSRF checks. It returns server-derived order information without payment.

Request fields read directly: `code`, `token`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

Response: JSON success/error or message data; payload keys directly constructed include `success`, `code`, `message`, `token`, `merchant`, `description`, `amount`, `expires_at`, `seconds_left`. Role guards may redirect before JSON output.

CSRF verification occurs in this file; branch-specific scope applies where described above.

Request: the current session and any shared-helper context; no direct named request field is read by this file.

Response: HTML page or redirect with validation/session feedback.

### 2.10 Audit and Email Infrastructure

#### a. Module Description

The infrastructure module records security and business audit events and delivers transactional email. It also contains machine-local configuration examples, the mail spool, and the command-line mail worker.

#### b. Features

Append-only audit. A dedicated audit connection checks its required schema and appends redacted event data. A database advisory lock serializes a SHA-256 previous-hash chain; legacy rows without hashes are identified as unverifiable. Correlation identifiers, endpoint, method, outcome, actor role, target, and hashed session references support traceability.

Transaction-aware logging. Audit calls associated with an active PDO transaction are queued and are flushed or discarded by the commit/rollback wrappers and shutdown handling. The audit viewer requires finance and super-administrator authorization and supports filters and chain verification.

Audit installation. The command-line installer defines the additional columns, restricted database account, and update/delete blocking triggers. Its existence does not establish that its privileges or triggers are deployed. The runtime logger does not install these structures automatically.

SMTP delivery. PHPMailer sends UTF-8 HTML messages through configured authenticated SMTP, with Gmail STARTTLS on port 587 in the supplied transport setup and a ten-second timeout. Queueing writes JSON spool records and attempts to start a background worker, with synchronous fallback when queuing fails.

Mail worker. The CLI-only worker acquires a file lock, processes a bounded run, retries up to three attempts with delay, recovers stale sending records, and retains failed records and logs. A queued message is not evidence of successful external delivery.

#### c. Functions and Methods

Signatures identify explicit inputs; handlers also consume enclosing session, request, DOM, or service state. Anonymous functions are identified by source line and, where available, JavaScript offset. Callback return values belong to the enclosing operation. SQL-table references below are direct references; shared service calls can use additional tables.

##### admin/audit_log.php

- **audit_e** — `admin/audit_log.php:359`. Inputs/signature: `function audit_e($value): string`. Implements the audit e operation in this file. Outputs: declared `string`; the computed expression or delegated result.

#### d. Database Tables Used

- **merchant_wallets**. Stores the merchant owner's balance. user_id identifies users; purchase, settlement, and merchant-funded load movements reference its wallet id. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `balance`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **p2p_transfers**. Stores peer-transfer attribution, amount, message/reference, and timing in association with student wallets or users and the transaction ledger. Key declared columns: `id`, `amount`, `status`, `reference_no`, `from_wallet_id`, `to_wallet_id`, `from_user_id`, `to_user_id`, `message`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **student_wallets**. Stores the student user's balance, freeze flag, and spending controls. user_id identifies users; current transactions and peer transfers attribute movements to this wallet. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `balance`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `daily_spend_limit`, `is_frozen`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **systemic_audit_trail**. Stores redacted actor/action/target events, old/new serialized values, request context, outcome, and chained hashes. User attribution is nullable for unknown or pre-authentication actors. Key declared columns: `user_id`, `log_id`, `user_role`, `action_type`, `stall_id`, `affected_table`, `old_value`, `new_value`, `ip_address`, `user_agent`, `timestamp`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **transactions**. Stores the current referenced wallet ledger, including type, amount, status, fees, initiating user, wallet attribution, and school-year context. Optional student, merchant, and parent wallet identifiers distinguish the movement. Key declared columns: `id`, `student_wallet_id`, `merchant_wallet_id`, `transaction_type`, `amount`, `status`, `reference_no`, `initiated_by`, `voucher_id`, `vault_before`, `vault_after`, `total_in_circulation`, `notes`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **users**. Stores login identity, password hash, role/subrole, merchant ownership, profile, first-login flags, and account restrictions. userID is the principal identity referenced by wallets and role-specific records; roleID relates to role. Key declared columns: `userID`, `roleID`, `last_name`, `first_name`, `middle_name`, `suffix`, `contact_number`, `email`, `password`, `mint_pin`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.

#### e. API Endpoints and HTTP Entry Points

Routes are relative to the application base URL. The method notation identifies the request inputs consumed by the implementation; it does not imply a universal method-rejection guard. Where GET and POST are merged, both can supply an action. Each PHP file is counted once as an entry point; its action variants are listed separately.

##### GET /admin/audit_log.php

Source: `admin/audit_log.php`. Finance and super_admin. Displays filtered audit events, supports AJAX table refresh, and performs requested chain verification.

Request fields read directly: `action_type`, `actor`, `ajax`, `amount`, `correlation_id`, `date_from`, `date_to`, `items`, `merchant_user_id`, `merchant_wallet_id`, `notes`, `outcome`, `page`, `reference_no`, `status`, `student_user_id`, `student_wallet_id`, `target`, `total_in_circulation`, `transaction_type`, `user_role`, `vault_after`, `vault_before`, `verify`, `voucher_id`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

Response: HTML audit page or AJAX-rendered row fragment and verification feedback.

##### GET /admin/view_audit.php

Source: `admin/view_audit.php`. Finance and super_admin. Displays a signed audit-event detail record.

Request fields read directly: `token`. Shared helpers may additionally read csrf_token or profile fields.

Response: HTML page or redirect with validation/session feedback.

### 2.11 Shared Presentation and Browser Components

#### a. Module Description

The presentation module supplies shared role navigation, layout fragments, styling, and browser components. PHP includes adapt headers and navigation to the signed-in role; common scripts implement interaction conventions used by the pages.

#### b. Features

Layout and navigation. Includes render document heads, role headers, sidebars, footers, alerts, and repeated form or profile fragments. The loaded interface assets provide responsive navigation, tables, icons, dialogs, and charts.

Browser interaction. Page-local and shared JavaScript handle data fetching, modal state, form submission, filtering, sorting, image previews, QR display or scanning, and notification refresh. Their functions are catalogued with the page or asset that defines them.

Bundled components. Minified Bootstrap JavaScript contains component lifecycle, event, placement, focus, keyboard, and utility routines. The function catalogue preserves source locations and callable identity, including anonymous callbacks; shortened internal identifiers do not establish a separate business feature.

Static design assets. Stylesheets, icons, imagery, and the theme document define visual presentation. Image semantics are [unverified] where assets are binary; file-level coverage is recorded in the appendix.

#### c. Functions and Methods

Signatures identify explicit inputs; handlers also consume enclosing session, request, DOM, or service state. Anonymous functions are identified by source line and, where available, JavaScript offset. Callback return values belong to the enclosing operation. SQL-table references below are direct references; shared service calls can use additional tables.

#### d. Database Tables Used

- **notifications**. Stores recipient-specific in-application notices, type/icon/title/body, target link, and read state. user_id identifies the recipient. Key declared columns: `id`, `user_id`, `type`, `icon`, `title`, `message`, `link`, `is_read`, `created_at`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.
- **users**. Stores login identity, password hash, role/subrole, merchant ownership, profile, first-login flags, and account restrictions. userID is the principal identity referenced by wallets and role-specific records; roleID relates to role. Key declared columns: `userID`, `roleID`, `last_name`, `first_name`, `middle_name`, `suffix`, `contact_number`, `email`, `password`, `mint_pin`. Full column and relationship inventory: Section 4.

#### e. API Endpoints and HTTP Entry Points

This module defines no directly routed application HTTP endpoint. Includes and services are called by the entry points catalogued in the other modules.

### 2.12 Database Installation and Legacy Compatibility

#### a. Module Description

The database module supplies the SQL installation history, migrations, administrative installers, and sample import material. These files define both current structures and historical structures retained by the application or dump.

#### b. Features

Installation and migration. SQL files create and alter wallet, merchant, application, parent, enrollment, tenancy, audit, and financial structures. PHP runtime ensure-functions supplement these definitions when features are accessed.

Legacy models. Singular transaction, topup, wallet, merchant_accounts, student_fees, tuition_credits, payment_verifications, vouchers, and related tables remain represented in repository schema or reporting adapters. Their presence does not establish an active user interface for each former workflow.

Database objects. SQL defines four views, six wallet/cap/voucher triggers, two audit immutability triggers, and a temporary add_index_if_missing procedure. Some migrations replace or remove earlier definitions; installation order and deployed activation are [unverified].

Operational utilities. The audit installer configures schema and privileges. The profile seeding utility derives demonstration profile data and can preserve existing values or force replacement; it invokes schema helpers even along its dry-run path. Neither utility is executed for this inventory.

### 2.13 Vendored PHPMailer

#### a. Module Description

The vendored PHPMailer library constructs and sends MIME messages and implements SMTP, POP-before-SMTP, OAuth token adaptation, exception formatting, and supporting transport utilities. The application invokes its mail-construction and SMTP transport interfaces through connection/mailer.php.

#### b. Features

Message composition. PHPMailer manages addresses, headers, text and HTML alternatives, attachments, encodings, MIME boundaries, language messages, signing, and transport selection. The repository application uses a subset of these capabilities; library availability alone does not establish application use.

SMTP transport. SMTP implements connection establishment, greeting, capability parsing, TLS, authentication, command exchange, message data transfer, reset, and termination. POP3 provides optional authorization against a POP server.

OAuth and compatibility. OAuth adapts a provider token into the XOAUTH2 value expected by SMTP, while OAuthTokenProvider declares its contract. DSNConfigurator maps connection-string options to mailer properties. External provider classes required by optional OAuth use are not supplied by a root Composer installation.

#### c. Functions and Methods

Signatures identify explicit inputs; handlers also consume enclosing session, request, DOM, or service state. Anonymous functions are identified by source line and, where available, JavaScript offset. Callback return values belong to the enclosing operation. SQL-table references below are direct references; shared service calls can use additional tables.

### 2.14 Documentation, Media, and Tooling

#### a. Module Description

The support module contains project prose, diagrams and reference material, screenshots, uploaded files, generated promotional composition files, and duplicated local skill packages. These files support the project but do not constitute additional wallet HTTP features.

#### b. Features

Project documentation. Manuscript, manual, design, theme, and diagram material describe aspects of the system at different development stages. Where prose references removed routes or different fee behavior, the executable implementation controls this inventory.

Media composition. The Hyperframes package contains a timed HTML composition, assets, package scripts, and composition guidance. Its browser functions drive animation and layout rather than wallet transactions.

Audio analysis tools. Each copy of the brag skill includes Python functions for argument handling, audio loading, timing and energy analysis, cue detection, serialization, and command-line reporting. The duplicated files are counted separately because both exist in the working tree.

Uploads and local support files. Uploaded images and PDF files, screenshots, spool support files, local tool settings, and lockfiles are inventoried without exposing personal content or configured credentials. Their binary semantic contents remain [unverified].

#### c. Functions and Methods

Signatures identify explicit inputs; handlers also consume enclosing session, request, DOM, or service state. Anonymous functions are identified by source line and, where available, JavaScript offset. Callback return values belong to the enclosing operation. SQL-table references below are direct references; shared service calls can use additional tables.

## 3. Cross-Cutting Concerns

### 3.1 Authentication, authorization, and session state

record.php uses password_verify for login; the supported path does not compare a submitted password directly with a plaintext database value. connection/app.php establishes regenerated sessions, implements selector/validator remembered login, and checks role, account activity, lockout, inherited merchant restriction, and forced password-change state. A remembered validator is stored as a hash. Login failures, blocked correct-password attempts, and denied privileged operations have audit paths.

Authorization remains local to each entry point and action. Merchant ownership resolution associates staff with their owner's inventory and wallet; parent–student link checks delimit supervision; signed detail tokens are verified with a scope-specific HMAC. A signed token contains no expiry and is not an independent permission grant. admin/api/economy.php checks finance for top-up and settlement operations but its pay branch accepts supplied wallet identifiers under the session check without an additional branch-specific role or ownership check. The route catalogue records this implemented distinction.

CSRF enforcement is selective. It occurs in student and parent checkout, QR validation, student transfer, allowance, waiver claim, business-profile changes, selected staff changes, notification read marking, and finance settings. Merchant QR-order creation also verifies a token. Cart mutation handlers and several finance, parent-control, profile-image, merchant-profile, and inventory handlers do not call the shared verifier. A token included by browser code does not by itself establish server verification.

### 3.2 Financial consistency and account controls

connection/CirculationEngine.php uses database transactions, settings-row locking, guarded balance updates, reference generation, and ledger insertion for its value movements. The current circulation invariant includes parent-wallet balances in addition to the vault, student and merchant wallets, and eligible legacy vouchers. database SQL views contain earlier circulation definitions that omit parent wallets; their results are not assumed equivalent to the current PHP calculation.

Student and parent checkout lock the current buyer's pending cart and obtain the payable amount from stored order data. Server checks revalidate merchant identity, inventory availability, quantities, balance, and applicable account restrictions before completion. Student peer transfer and allowance use the corresponding account and relationship checks. Maintenance-fee accrual is distinct from wallet debit, and remittance reporting is distinct from settlement.

admin/release_encashment.php calls the settlement engine before updating the encashment request. The engine completes its own transaction, so the subsequent request update is a separate database step. Pending encashment creation does not reserve funds. These statements describe the transaction boundaries visible in the implementation.

### 3.3 Audit logging

connection/audit_logger.php uses separate configured audit credentials, recursive sensitive-field redaction, canonical JSON, request correlation, outcome and reason fields, and hashed session references. Actor identity can be absent for pre-authentication events. The recorded network address comes from REMOTE_ADDR rather than an arbitrary client-supplied forwarding value.

The append path serializes the previous-hash lookup and new entry with an advisory lock. Chain verification detects mismatched hashes or predecessor links and identifies legacy unhashed entries. Application transaction wrappers coordinate queued audit events with commit and rollback. database/migrations/audit_hardening.php defines the required schema, SELECT/INSERT audit permissions, and triggers that reject update or deletion; deployed installation is [unverified]. The runtime logger checks schema health instead of performing privileged installation.

### 3.4 Uploads and document delivery

apply_upload.php and connection/app.php validate application document categories, extension/media rules, upload state, and maximum size before staging files in a random-token draft directory. Final application submission moves the staged directory into the application's upload location. Contract and waiver uploads, merchant compliance files, logos, and profile photographs have separate handlers and limits. Application, contract, and waiver document paths commonly use a five-megabyte limit; profile photographs use two megabytes. Accepted types remain specific to each field.

admin/doc.php normalizes the requested path, rejects invalid traversal forms, resolves the real path beneath the permitted upload root, and applies finance or student/parent waiver authorization before presenting a document. merchant/contract.php and merchant/doc.php constrain file access to the merchant owner. Image previews and PDF streams use different response handling. Uploaded binary contents are not treated as application source and their semantic contents are [unverified] in this inventory.

### 3.5 Error handling and configuration

connection/app.php distinguishes intended runtime/validation messages from unexpected or PDO failures through gjc_safe_error. JSON handlers return success flags with message, error, or code fields; individual handlers set HTTP error status selectively. Role guards can redirect before a handler emits JSON. Several compatibility DDL paths catch an error and continue, so a source declaration does not prove successful alteration in a particular database.

Environment/local configuration resolves database credentials, SMTP credentials, dedicated audit access, and the signed-view secret. No configured secret value or database seed record is reproduced. connection/config.php derives URL constants from the incoming request and applies Asia/Manila time. The application relies on PDO parameter binding for values in its prepared queries and uses server-side validation in financial, upload, account, and ownership operations.

### 3.6 Web-server and output controls

The root .htaccess supplies extensionless routing, selected canonical redirects, directory access restrictions, disabled directory listing, and response headers including frame, content-type, XSS, and referrer controls. Sensitive paths include connection, database, includes, uploads, storage, docs, screenshots, and PHPMailer. Dotfiles and selected source/document extensions are also denied. The explicit API canonicalization exclusions cover admin, student, and merchant API paths; parent API paths are not in that same exclusion list. HTTPS forcing and custom error-page directives remain commented.

HTML escaping is performed at individual rendering sites where their code calls an escaping function. The shared function named gjc_e only casts to string. Its name therefore does not establish output escaping for a caller.

### 3.7 Background and request-driven work

connection/mailer.php queues JSON mail records, starts connection/mail_worker.php when possible, and can fall back to synchronous SMTP delivery. The CLI worker uses a file lock, a bounded approximately 120-second run, three attempts with a fifteen-second retry delay, and recovery of sending files older than 300 seconds. Failed records and worker logs remain under the spool storage. An HTTP request to the worker is rejected.

Suspension expiry, overdue application expiry, stale draft cleanup, rent reminders, and eligible fee collection run when their calling request invokes the helper. The repository does not supply a general cron scheduler or recurring allowance worker. External SMTP availability and message delivery are [unverified].

## 4. Database Summary

### 4.1 Interpretation of schema evidence

The catalogue contains every distinct table name declared by CREATE TABLE in SQL or PHP, with additional literal ALTER declarations and runtime column-definition maps. It presents the union of repository versions rather than a claim that mutually different definitions coexist in one database. Types, defaults, keys, and sources are retained where declared. Conditional migrations, dynamic enumeration expansion, and installation order determine the deployed result, which is [unverified].

Relationships described as logical follow application identifiers and joins. Only clauses explicitly declaring FOREIGN KEY establish schema-level foreign-key evidence. The presence of a user_id or wallet_id column alone does not establish an enforced constraint. Seed data and credentials are excluded from this structural catalogue.

### 4.2 Entity relationships

users is the identity hub. role supplies historical role identifiers; student_info associates a student identity with course and graduation information; role-specific wallets associate users with student and merchant balances. parents associates a parent user with a parent record, parent_wallets gives that record an independent balance, and parent_student_links creates the many-to-many supervision relation with student users. parent_alerts records events within that relation.

transactions is the current financial ledger. Its nullable student_wallet_id, merchant_wallet_id, and parent_wallet_id fields identify the participating wallet classes according to transaction type, while initiated-by and school-year fields provide actor and academic context. p2p_transfers adds peer-transfer attribution, fee_revenue_log records service-fee allocation, and cap_increase_log records issuance. system_settings holds the cap and vault; app_settings holds configurable rules. Older transaction, topup, wallet, voucher, and revenue structures remain separate compatibility entities.

merchant_inventory belongs to the merchant owner and supplies order item data. merchant_qr_orders and cart_orders retain order state and item snapshots; cart_orders distinguishes student and parent buyers. sales_remittances records reporting boundaries. Merchant account records relate users to business identity and stalls; staff ownership is represented on users.

stall_applications relates an applicant to a preferred or awarded stall and, after provisioning, to a merchant user. It stores appointment, document, contract, and initial rental-payment evidence. merchant_leases relates the owner and stall to a dated rental agreement; merchant_rent_payments is its one-to-many receipt collection. merchant_documents stores replaceable compliance documents, merchant_card_views stores review timestamps, and archived_rejections preserves declined application information.

school_years has one-to-many enrollment and balance-snapshot records. student_enrollments has one logical record per student and school year, and enrollment_roster_staging holds proposed batch rows before application. fee_waiver_credits holds the student's credit state and fee_waiver_credit_logs records its changes. maintenance_fees relates assessed charges to the student and transaction reference; maintenance_fee_collections groups collected rows under receipts.

notifications and systemic_audit_trail cross module boundaries. Notification rows belong to a recipient. Audit rows associate an optional actor and target with a request and a predecessor hash; the target-table/target-id context is an application-level polymorphic reference rather than a foreign key to every possible target.

### 4.4 Runtime alterations and lifecycle distinctions

The shared user-schema helpers extend users with restricted-product strike fields, finance suspension/ban fields, position and staff_removed_at, first-login flags, and profile sex/date/address fields. They widen status to include Suspended and Banned, and allow nullable middle_name and suffix where required. The profile helper stores date of birth rather than a separately maintained age. Source: `connection/app.php`.

The stall workflow helper adds meeting, document, contract, award, cancellation, and view fields; it can rename gender to sex and remap legacy pipeline statuses to pending_verification, awarded, rejected, cancelled, and expired. The current_step and older payment/temporary-password fields remain compatibility columns. The presence of temp_password or temp_password_plain is documented structurally; no stored value is reproduced. Source: `connection/app.php`.

Runtime order changes add merchant_qr_orders.items_json and short_code with a unique index, and add parent attribution and buyer_role to cart_orders while permitting null student references. Wallet and ledger helpers add parent-wallet attribution, fee fields, school-year attribution, and required transaction enumeration values. Parent controls extend student-wallet freeze and spending-limit fields. Sources: `connection/app.php`, `database/scan_pay_migration.sql`.

Other runtime additions include maintenance_fees.collection_id, merchant_leases.rent_reminder_period, roster staging status, registry parent details, and merchant.notes. Audit installation separately adds target/outcome/reason/subrole/request/session/hash context, widens payload and action columns, and changes actor nullability. Dynamic enumeration and column-name substitutions are reported here rather than treated as literal deployed SQL. Sources: `connection/app.php`, `admin/maintenance.php`, `database/migrations/audit_hardening.php`.

### 4.5 Views, triggers, and stored procedure

- **PROCEDURE add_index_if_missing**. Accepts table, index, and column-definition inputs, checks information_schema, executes an index creation when absent, and is dropped after the migration. Source: `database/merchant_tenant_directory_migration.sql:40`.
- **TRIGGER trg_block_expired_voucher_use**. Rejects voucher use when the stored expiry/status condition disallows it. Source: `database/dropped_views_triggers_backup.sql:18`, `database/voucher_patch.sql:57`, `database/voucher_schema.sql:97`, `database/voucher_triggers.sql:6`.
- **TRIGGER trg_guard_merchant_balance**. Rejects negative merchant balances and applies the historical aggregate-circulation guard. Source: `database/dropped_views_triggers_backup.sql:30`, `database/economy_migrations.sql:131`.
- **TRIGGER trg_guard_student_balance**. Rejects negative student balances and applies the historical aggregate-circulation guard. Source: `database/dropped_views_triggers_backup.sql:58`, `database/economy_migrations.sql:92`.
- **TRIGGER trg_guard_transaction_cap**. Rejects ledger insertion when recorded circulation exceeds the cap plus the one-cent tolerance. Source: `database/dropped_views_triggers_backup.sql:86`, `database/economy_migrations.sql:64`.
- **TRIGGER trg_guard_vault_update**. Rejects vault values exceeding the cap and rejects cap decreases. Source: `database/dropped_views_triggers_backup.sql:100`, `database/token_economy_schema.sql:234`.
- **TRIGGER trg_recycle_expired_voucher**. Returns remaining value to the vault on expiry; later definitions restrict this recycling to nonrefundable vouchers. Source: `database/dropped_views_triggers_backup.sql:115`, `database/token_economy_schema.sql:265`, `database/voucher_patch.sql:77`, `database/voucher_schema.sql:119`, `database/voucher_triggers.sql:18`.
- **VIEW v_circulation_health**. Compares the historical circulation snapshot with the cap and reports health/difference information. Source: `database/dropped_views_triggers_backup.sql:5`, `database/economy_migrations.sql:166`.
- **VIEW v_circulation_snapshot**. Aggregates the historical vault, student, merchant, and active-voucher circulation model; its definition omits parent-wallet balances. Source: `database/dropped_views_triggers_backup.sql:8`, `database/token_economy_schema.sql:288`.
- **VIEW v_p2p_daily_totals**. Aggregates daily peer-transfer totals for the historical reporting model. Source: `database/dropped_views_triggers_backup.sql:11`, `database/migration_v2.sql:278`.
- **VIEW v_vouchers_active**. Selects vouchers considered active under the stored view criteria. Source: `database/dropped_views_triggers_backup.sql:14`, `database/voucher_patch.sql:96`, `database/voucher_schema.sql:140`.

The audit trigger names are constructed by the PHP installer and are documented separately below. Existing definitions, replacements, drops, and the database dump are alternative repository states, not evidence of concurrent deployment.

- **TRIGGER trg_audit_no_update**. Rejects updates to audit records using a database signal. Source: `database/migrations/audit_hardening.php`.
- **TRIGGER trg_audit_no_delete**. Rejects deletion of audit records using a database signal. Source: `database/migrations/audit_hardening.php`.

### Coverage limitations and excluded material

No working-tree text file is skipped. All 810 binary assets are included individually in Appendix A and are read for integrity and type/size accounting; their image, audio, video, and PDF semantic contents are [unverified]. Consequently, the file inventory is complete, while cover-to-cover semantic review of those binary assets is not claimed. The per-file binary marking is the complete list of this limitation.

The .git directory is excluded as version-control metadata. No application source, local configuration, hidden skill package, ignored SQL dump, upload, screenshot, or generated composition file is excluded from the working-tree inventory. Live database contents, installed triggers/privileges, external SMTP delivery, CDN responses, and browser execution are [unverified], because this analysis does not run the application or alter its data.

Read-only analysis uses filesystem reads, PHP tokenization, JavaScript syntax parsing, Python AST parsing, and SQL declaration inspection. It does not invoke request handlers, connect to the database, execute migrations, launch mail delivery, or run media publication commands. SYSTEM_DOCUMENTATION.md is the sole intended output file.

### Final reconciliation

The final catalogue contains all 2,034 extracted callable definitions, all 118 routed application entry-point files, all 61 declared table names, and all 1,121 pre-existing working-tree files. JavaScript parsing and Python AST extraction complete without parse errors; PHP definitions are extracted by tokenization. The SQL catalogue also identifies four implemented views, eight trigger names, and one temporary procedure.

A SHA-256 comparison against the read-only inventory baseline finds zero changed, added, or removed pre-existing working-tree files. SYSTEM_DOCUMENTATION.md is the only newly created analysis output. The pre-existing untracked brag-output directory remains unchanged. No application execution or database mutation is performed.
